name: Meta AI

type.note: One humanist variable family throughout. Rail titles 36/~46 at 500, uppercase 14px eyebrows in accent blue, labels ~700 only inside buttons and links.

thesis: A two-column page where a pinned left rail holds each section's title and CTA while large rounded media scroll past on the right, all in one blue.
why_made: Every section repeats one grid (rail at x=32, media column from x=384) with hairlines and a single accent, so video and photography can be loud while the interface stays quiet.
watch_out: The pale-blue media ring turns into a dated glow border if thickened or applied to every card, and the pinned rail looks empty without strong media beside it.

name: Hims

type.note: Headlines split into two colours per clause. Scale: 44 section, 28 card, 19-20 tile, 12-13 legal. The serif wordmark is the only serif on the page.

thesis: A telehealth store built as a stack of full-bleed rounded colour rooms, each tinted from its product photography, with the nav recolouring to match.
why_made: Colour comes out of the photography instead of a fixed brand palette, so each room feels art-directed, while a tiny kit of 24px cards, 48px pills and two-tone headlines holds the variety together.
watch_out: Stock photos or section colours not sampled from the image break it instantly, and tone-on-tone cards turn into muddy brown boxes without real art direction.

name: Ro

type.note: -3% tracking at every display size: 72, 46/600 for H1 emphasis, 41/-1.23px H2. Body stays 13-18px.

thesis: A telehealth storefront led by tightly cropped hands-and-pills photography on matched grey-blue backdrops, with pale yellow as the only accent.
why_made: Consistent macro photography and an 80px pill control system make a dense, disclaimer-heavy catalogue look calm.
watch_out: Sharp image tiles beside 24px hero cards show an unresolved radius system, and the mix looks careless without this level of photography.

name: Canva

type.note: H2 64 at -0.64px, tile titles 28. Regular weight on loud colour keeps it friendly. Mobile capture is a Cloudflare check page, so desktop only.

thesis: A maximalist product tour where a vertical purple-to-teal wash and saturated gradient tiles show the variety of what people can make.
why_made: Every tile follows one strict formula (title, small white button, product scene cropped by the bottom edge) at a fixed 24px radius, so colour chaos sits on a rigid grid.
watch_out: Without real product scenes, rainbow gradient cards collapse into generic AI-startup noise.

name: Olipop

type.note: Fat retro serif for all headings, geometric Ano for everything else. H2 54, card heads ~28.

thesis: A soda store where the can artwork sets the whole system: retro fat serif, sticker-cut fruit and flat candy colour blocks.
why_made: Palette, type and illustration are lifted directly from the packaging, so the site reads as an extension of the can, and product renders stay the sharpest thing on screen.
watch_out: Fat retro serifs and sticker art become kiddie clip art unless packaging of this quality anchors them.

name: Replit Pricing

type.note: -6% tracking at display only. Tier names 32/700, FAQ 20/400. Prices stay small at 14px.

thesis: A short pricing page where each plan takes its own faint tint and button colour on warm off-white.
why_made: Three cards share exact row baselines, colour alone carries the hierarchy, and the FAQ is nothing but hairlines.
watch_out: Tinted cards with coloured buttons go toy-like if tints get stronger than a few percent saturation.

name: Insomnia

type.note: H2 36/700, Roboto Mono for checklist rows. Stock type; the product frames carry the identity.

thesis: A plain devtool landing page alternating white copy blocks with dark product frames and a deep violet accent.
why_made: Real product shots framed by one consistent violet rim with a spectrum edge carry the page and give it a recognisable object.
watch_out: Roboto Bold headlines and default bullets read as a 2019 template the moment the genuine product UI is removed.

name: Modern Treasury

type.note: H2 47/58.75. mt-mono at 10-13px uppercase handles labels, tags and code. mt-neue-text for card titles at 32px.

thesis: An infrastructure brand drawn like an engineering diagram: near-square controls, hairlines, mono tags and product fragments on warm paper.
why_made: Near-square controls, one muted green and tiny monospace labels signal ledger-grade precision, and every card illustration is true product vocabulary drawn in one small UI kit.
watch_out: With generic mock UI this becomes plain white-label SaaS, and square black buttons only look deliberate when the grid is exact.

name: Algolia

type.note: H2 52 at -1px. Tight bold Sora gives an engineered voice; Inter in small UI.

thesis: A dense enterprise nav over a navy rotating hero, then light sections that explain search through real results UI.
why_made: Deep #000033 anchors header and footer, and a realistic search mock makes an abstract product concrete.
watch_out: Two-tier nav, chat widget and auto-rotating hero compete, and copying all three makes any page feel like enterprise clutter.

name: Fundrise

type.note: Metropolis for tracked caps labels, Ivar Headline for card titles. Serif optical tightness does the tone work.

thesis: An investing platform borrowing the tone of a private bank: literary serif headlines, warm paper, rust accent and architectural photography.
why_made: The serif and sans pairing plus buildings-as-assets imagery establish trust, and clean white split cards keep each asset class plain.
watch_out: The long footnote wall and a nav that lets content collide with its links show how fast this slips toward a legal document.

name: Framer Templates

type.note: Interface scale only: nothing above 30px, so thumbnails stay the loudest thing. Weight 450 for labels.

thesis: A dark marketplace shell that stays out of the way so loud template thumbnails do the talking.
why_made: Tight 13-15px type, a #111 canvas and a strict four-up rhythm make hundreds of unrelated thumbnails read as one calm catalogue.
watch_out: With weak thumbnails the shell has nothing to offer and reads as an empty grey grid.

name: Przebiegły Team

type.note: One family, 900 caps against regular body. Custom groovy logos carry all the personality.

thesis: A Polish running coach's site built around sticker-style logos, camouflage texture and neon lime, like a race-kit brand.
why_made: The identity is real: hand-drawn wordmarks in several sticker versions, a consistent camo and one neon accent, with simple layouts so the marks can shout.
watch_out: Camo and neon over plain Inter becomes a Canva flyer the moment the custom marks are absent.

name: Shopify Polaris

type.note: URL redirects to shopify.dev/docs/api/polaris. Only 2 unique stops; page is 1915px tall.

thesis: A calm developer reference where a rounded floating sidebar and retro pixel icons give a standard docs shell some identity.
why_made: Consistent 8px radii, disciplined grey tiers and a quiet active state make navigation feel solid, and pixel-art icons give it a character most docs lack. It is competent system work rather than memorable design.
watch_out: The floating promo sticker covers content on phone, showing how a marketing add-on can undo a tidy docs layout.

name: Kinfolk

type.note: No bold anywhere. Hierarchy is case and size: caps topic line, sentence-case dek, same weight. Muted value is the hover-dimmed state, estimated.

thesis: A magazine rebuilt as a slow-paced print object, where commissioned photography and one serif do all the work on square white pages.
why_made: Every block has a different width and scale yet all share 34px gutters, one type voice and zero radius or shadow. Generous white gaps and exact image crops give the expensive pacing of a real issue.
watch_out: Without commissioned photography and a proprietary-feeling serif this is simply a white page with centred text.

name: Anthropic News

type.note: Sizes are a tight rem scale (13/15/17/21/26/33/42). anthropicMono appears only for counts and table headers.

thesis: A newsroom treated as a warm paper ledger: a broadsheet front page on top, a dense sortable table beneath, with all colour left to collage imagery.
why_made: Everything sits on a 16px-gap 1280px grid and one yellow-cast neutral ramp, so hierarchy comes from tone and weight with almost no shadow. Small behaviours, such as the row that grows past the table edge and the nav that re-themes over dark bands, show the finish.
watch_out: The pill nav and ivory ground become a generic Claude-beige template if the imagery is stock or the table loses its strict column positions.

name: Electron

type.note: Docusaurus base with system fonts; 900-weight H2s and light-weight hero headline. Links #028399.

thesis: An open-source framework homepage that dresses a docs-template base in navy and atom-cyan and proves the product with real app screenshots.
why_made: Live version numbers in the install terminal and the tilted backplates give it honest developer detail. It stays low silver: the system-font 900 headings, centred stacking and dead gaps still show the template.
watch_out: Default-weight system fonts and identical centred sections feel dated quickly; copy the backplate and terminal ideas, not the overall shell.

name: Sequoia

type.note: Three voices: Rosart serif for the one hero line, Unica77 for tile titles, Pitch Sans mono for nav and tags.

thesis: A venture firm's homepage as a cream content wall held together by print-style crop rails and one hand-drawn pen stroke.
why_made: The hairline rails that stop short of each tile give a generic two-up feed a printed, engineered feel, and the chalk line art adds a human hand. It misses gold because tile content is uneven, with third-party thumbnails and busy overlaid titles.
watch_out: White titles over unmanaged portraits lose legibility, and the rails look fussy if they are not exactly on the 16px grid.

name: Huel

type.note: One word in each heading swaps to suisseWorks italic; suisseIntlMono handles ticker and tags.

thesis: A direct-to-consumer nutrition store with Swiss bones: black, cream and white blocks, and studio product photography doing the selling.
why_made: Consistent 1152px container, 8px and pill radii, and a strict heading rule with one italic serif word make a dense retail page feel designed. Studio product shots on matched orange and cream sets lift it well above a stock Shopify theme.
watch_out: Stack ticker, promo chips, quiz pill and chat button together as here and the top of the page turns noisy; the italic word trick also wears out if used without a real serif.

name: FigJam

type.note: Regular weight at huge size; hand-lettered marker font inside the product shots only. figmaMono for chips.

thesis: A whiteboard product page that behaves like a whiteboard: sticker collage, stickies, live cursors and pastel bands on stark black-and-white type.
why_made: Rigid 60px gutters and plain black controls hold the noise in check, and the demos are rebuilt product UI running live rather than screenshots. The colour is loud but always assigned to a job, separating feature groups.
watch_out: Without a playful product to justify it, this collage and pastel mix becomes childish clip art, so it suits a brief that asks for energy, not a default.

name: Work & Co

type.note: Two families with one job each: grotesk for labels and titles, Garamond for every reading sentence.

thesis: An agency homepage reduced to a typeset index: one offset grid, two typefaces, one red.
why_made: Every block hangs from the same x=550 edge in a 1060px container, and the serif and grotesk pairing gives contrast without a single size or colour trick. Restraint this complete only works because spacing, rules and link behaviour are exact.
watch_out: With weak type or looser alignment this reads as an unstyled document, so the fonts and the single left edge are not optional.

name: Martin Development

type.note: Bogart Alt Light serif appears only in tiny utility lines such as 'Scroll to Discover' and the copyright.

thesis: A regional property developer turned into a poster: a 400px navy wordmark that sits inside the house photograph, then slides across the page.
why_made: The depth mask between sky and roofline is cleanly cut, and the loud wordmark is balanced by a calm cream page with hairline columns and inked site plans. Scale is the idea, and everything else stays quiet to let it land.
watch_out: Giant type behind a badly masked subject looks like a template trick; the cut-out must be pixel clean and the scale must truly overflow.

name: Zed Docs

type.note: Lilex for code. Serif headings over a duospaced body give an engineering-manual voice.

thesis: Documentation that reads like a well-set engineering manual: paper ground, serif headings, duospaced body and one blue.
why_made: The three-font pairing and faint paper grain set it apart from every Docusaurus clone, and small rules such as solid versus dashed heading lines show typographic care. Body contrast and wide tracking keep it short of top tier for reading comfort.
watch_out: Wide-tracked mono-style body gets tiring fast; it only works with generous 26px leading and a short measure.

name: Fly.io Blog

type.note: Hero background is an image; plum estimated ~#281950. Measured mobile overflow on this page.

thesis: An infrastructure blog with the personality of a picture book, where custom illustrated art on every post turns a card grid into a gallery.
why_made: A custom illustration for every post is the investment that makes it, and the plain white card system stays disciplined so the art can be as wild as it likes. Soft serif titles keep the technical content warm.
watch_out: The card grid is ordinary on its own; with stock or AI filler art instead of a committed illustrator, nothing remains.

name: Airbnb

type.note: Desktop capture is held by a first-visit modal: 1 unique stop, page 900px. Elements come from the frame behind the scrim, the skeleton frame and phone frames.

thesis: A search-first marketplace app where a pill search bar and tightly packed photo rails do everything, warmed by rendered 3D icons.
why_made: Skeletons match final layout exactly and listing cards are ruthlessly simple, showing a product team that has refined these parts for years. A modal blocked the desktop page, so only the first screen and phone views could be judged.
watch_out: Photo-card density depends on real user imagery; rendered icons turn kitsch if lighting and scale are inconsistent.

name: Seed

type.note: Light weight 350 at display size keeps a clinical voice. Seed Sans Mono is used only on science labels.

thesis: Clinical supplements sold through moody tonal-green product still life and laboratory-style labelling.
why_made: A tight tonal system of dark greens with one lime accent, and jars lit like a perfume ad, give it a premium read. The capture is cut short by a marketing modal after two stops, so only the first third of the page could be judged, which holds it at silver.
watch_out: Tone-on-tone green cards rely entirely on the jar photography; with weaker product shots the page turns murky.

name: Snow Peak

type.note: Copy is pure black throughout with no muted tone. Capture is blocked by a newsletter modal from the third stop, so only the top of the page was judged.

thesis: A heritage camping brand sold through dusk photography, old-style serif headlines and hard-edged rectangles.
why_made: Radius 0 everywhere, one serif and one sans, and photography good enough to need no decoration. Wide fixed-width buttons give it a print-ad cadence.
watch_out: Without photography this good, a serif on a darkened hero photo turns into a generic lifestyle Shopify theme.

name: CleanShot X

type.note: One family at 7 sizes; 15px weight 550 for all UI labels. H2 40/48 at 600.

thesis: A Mac utility sold by showing its own controls at poster scale inside a disciplined gradient bento.
why_made: Every tile holds a real control rather than a screenshot, and all gradients come from one peach-periwinkle-indigo family on a strict 20/14 radius system. Spacing never drifts from the 1192px frame.
watch_out: Gradient tiles without real UI fragments, or with hues from outside one family, collapse into generic AI-startup bento.

name: Meridian

type.note: Measured H1 56px and H2 32-40px do not match the 1440 hero, which renders ~80/80; Haffer SemiMono 12-14px uppercase for labels and buttons.

thesis: A clinic phone agent told as calm through one living orange shader wrapped around a warm cream page.
why_made: The shader, logo and footer wordmark share a single cell-line motif, and every neutral carries the same orange undertone. Lenis scrubbing makes the type reveal feel deliberate.
watch_out: Pale yellow on orange is weak for contrast, and a stray line-leading comma in the hero subhead shows how fragile centred type is; several cards are blank in this capture.

name: Khan Academy

type.note: Top of the capture is an unsupported-browser notice plus a donation takeover; the real homepage begins at the first scroll stop.

thesis: A nonprofit that routes each visitor by role and keeps a huge product warm through one flat illustration language.
why_made: The illustration system is consistent from hero to footer, and the role picker solves the real problem of mixed audiences. Controls are plain and clearly stated.
watch_out: Bright flat shapes plus a bold rounded sans fall into childish edtech template quickly without a real mascot and system.

name: Vercel AI SDK

type.note: Geist Mono for commands and code; H2 48/56 at -2.88px. Syntax colours are the only hues on the page.

thesis: An SDK page that lets code, install commands and copy buttons act as both the content and the decoration.
why_made: Every block is a usable tool, not an illustration of one, and a single 24px-gutter grid runs from logo to footer. Weight 450 with -6% tracking gives it an engineered voice.
watch_out: Without real product substance this monochrome hairline formula becomes an empty wireframe that looks like every Geist clone.

name: Vercel AI

type.note: H2 56/56 at -3.36px. Geist Mono only inside UI fragments.

thesis: A platform page that trusts near-empty space, Geist and small hairline illustrations to carry an enterprise pitch.
why_made: The hairline tile illustrations are excellent, drawn with real type and real logos. It stops short of gold because long stretches are unanchored copy with a third of the frame unresolved.
watch_out: Emptiness only works with this type control and customer list; copied without them it reads as an unfinished page.

name: Monocle

type.note: Wordmark drawn in Plantin caps; Helvetica Neue 13/700 uppercase for all UI, so reading text and controls never mix.

thesis: A magazine front page translated to the web with rules, columns and one yellow.
why_made: A strict ruled grid and a two-typeface split do all the work, and a house illustration style makes it unmistakable. The ads and density keep it from top tier.
watch_out: Ruled columns and a serif need real editorial volume and photography; on thin content it looks like a dated news theme.

name: Bellroy

type.note: One superfamily from ultra-heavy uppercase to fine tracked 11px labels.

thesis: A carry brand mixing tactile studio product shots with a maker's graph-paper notebook and a very heavy display face.
why_made: The contrast between ultra-black headlines and fine tracked UI gives it a voice, and graph paper with cut-out objects is ownable. Retail density and many section styles keep it short of top tier.
watch_out: Ultra-heavy caps over photos look cheap on weak imagery and need real tonal gradients behind them to stay legible.

name: Warp Pricing

type.note: Azeret Semi Mono for nav and buttons, Matter Mono in the footer; lavender #CBB0F7 is the data accent, yellow #EEF17C the action accent.

thesis: A dense pricing page made calm by square black actions, zero shadows and a single geometric display face.
why_made: Five plans and dozens of rows stay readable because each mark has one job: lavender means included, dotted underline means explained, square black means buy. Separation comes from tints and hairlines, never elevation.
watch_out: Four typefaces hold together only under strict role assignment; used loosely they look like a font sample.

name: Zapier

type.note: Serrif at ~40px is a second display voice for product explainers and quotes; Inter handles all UI.

thesis: A warm enterprise rebrand built from cream paper, black outlines, one orange and smeared landscape photography.
why_made: The blurred photo plates give product demos an ownable ground, and the serif and sans split gives the page two voices. Busy nav and many section treatments keep it below gold.
watch_out: Blurred photo backdrops turn muddy without grain and careful colour; two display faces need a strict rule for who speaks when.

name: xtrackr

type.note: All lowercase; weight 800 reserved for the one swapped brand word.

thesis: A subscription tracker sold through one sentence: lowercase light-weight type on near-black, with a bold brand name swapped into the headline.
why_made: One type voice (Manrope 300, lowercase) runs from hero to FAQ, and saturated gradient tiles are rationed against a near-black page. The rail nav, flip-board price and icon-grid closer each commit to a single idea.
watch_out: Weight 300 at 40% white on near-black goes illegible fast, and rainbow gradient tiles read as a template without strict pairing against dark phone tiles.

name: Cal.com Pricing

type.note: One family throughout; 14-16px does nearly all the work, sizes jump straight to 56-80px.

thesis: A pricing page that behaves like a product surface: one heavy geometric voice, a charcoal-on-white system, and a single inverted card.
why_made: Radii, button heights and text sizes sit on a tight scale, and the only spectacle is saved for the halftone footer wordmark. Small affordances such as dotted tooltip underlines and per-card switches show real product thinking.
watch_out: Heavy tight display type needs a well-drawn face; set in a generic bold grotesk the page collapses into a default shadcn pricing template.

name: VS Code

type.note: System fonts; headline scale stays small so the dark windows dominate.

thesis: The product is the page: working HTML replicas of the editor, in dark windows on calm grey, explain every feature.
why_made: Demos are live DOM with real syntax colour and typed text rather than screenshots, and system type with a single blue keeps attention on them. One 950px column holds everything together.
watch_out: Without genuinely working demos this becomes dark rectangles on grey, and small UI text inside scaled windows stops being legible.

name: Leeroy

type.note: Condensed high-contrast serif against tiny uppercase sans; scale jump is the signature.

thesis: An agency showcase as one continuous colour atmosphere: a blurred glow rises from the page floor and re-tints for each project.
why_made: A fine display serif, tiny uppercase sans and one electric blue hold steady while the atmosphere shifts. Hairline rows that draw in, hover inversions and a live clock show exacting detail.
watch_out: Without real client video and a genuinely fine serif, blurred gradient plus centred serif looks like any AI startup template.

name: Revena

type.note: Small display scale; custom diagrams carry impact instead of type.

thesis: Turns opaque hospital billing into a glowing green circuit where clinical documents flow into one AI mark.
why_made: One green family, film grain and custom diagrams give a small company a coherent product language, with every illustration sharing the same line, node and glow vocabulary.
watch_out: Green gradient plus grain plus glow goes muddy and low-contrast quickly, as the 12px labels here already show.

name: Struck

type.display: Plus Jakarta Sans, 56px/67px, 700, -3.36px; Poppins 49px/49px, 600, -1.96px in hero
type.note: Four families mixed (Space Grotesk, Poppins, Inter Tight, Plus Jakarta); the weakest part of the system.

thesis: A compliance AI framed like an architect's drawing: crop marks around every section on warm paper, with hot orange for action.
why_made: Corner-bracket frames carry one drawing-sheet idea across nav, hero, FAQ and footer, and the regulation library is a real working widget rather than a claim.
watch_out: Four typefaces and three bracket colours dilute the system, and brackets on everything quickly become decoration.

name: Reflect

type.note: AeonikPro only for headings; Inter carries everything else.

thesis: Note-taking positioned as cosmic: a violet eclipse of light recurs behind the product, and each section gets its own lit object.
why_made: Glow assets are rendered with real falloff while text and glass stay strictly disciplined, and sections earn distinct lit objects (planet limb, ciphertext halo, playable grid) rather than reusing one gradient.
watch_out: This is the most cloned dark-SaaS look; purple glow without original rendered assets reads instantly as a template.

name: Cursor Pricing

type.note: One custom family at weight 400 only; ink opacity does the job bold usually does.

thesis: A pricing page that removes everything except warm paper, one typeface and one dark button pointing at the recommended plan.
why_made: Only two radii, one weight and one saturated colour used once, with every section sharing the same 1300px edges. Restraint this complete only works because type and spacing are exact.
watch_out: Warm neutrals with default fonts read as beige and unfinished; the discipline only pays off with a distinctive typeface and exact spacing.

name: Nuro

type.note: Display caps at 48px across H1 and H2; mono only for metadata.

thesis: An autonomy company presented through large rounded media stages and calm, regular-weight sentences, letting vehicles and footage do the persuading.
why_made: Every page block shares one card anatomy, one 32px radius and one text inset, so wildly different imagery feels like one system. Exceptional photography and rendering stay uncluttered by type at a fixed 48px.
watch_out: Rounded image cards with average stock photography read as a template; the system needs art-directed media and strict text insets.

name: ReadMe

type.note: Italic coloured keywords inside serif headings carry the emphasis.

thesis: A documentation product drawn as a live blueprint: every section sits in the cells of one rounded grid that runs from white through navy to black.
why_made: One rounded-cell grid organises logos, features, quotes and code, square nodes mark focus points, and the serif italics add warmth to a technical system.
watch_out: Thin grid lines, faint mono labels and four floating overlays (video, ask bar, chat, nav) become noise; the grid must hold content or it is wallpaper.

name: Remix

type.note: Text glow via soft white shadow on headings only.

thesis: A web framework sold as a Y2K racing game: a particle world you fly through, an arcade italic wordmark and keyboard controls.
why_made: One fixed WebGL world holds every section while text panels stay conventional and very readable. Retro stickers, keyboard chips and the colour-cycling logo all belong to the same arcade idea.
watch_out: Without custom lettering and a real particle engine this collapses into neon clip art, and glow text only survives at very large sizes.

name: Chromatic

type.note: One rounded humanist family throughout; very open 1.75 body leading on dark; 14px caps with ~0.3em tracking for labels.

thesis: Explains a visual testing pipeline by literally running UI cards through a scanner under a calm slate-navy two-column page.
why_made: The hero strip turns the product's process into one moving diagram, and real, legible app screens carry every later section. The page keeps a strict 1080px container and plain two-column heading blocks.
watch_out: Friendly rounded type plus multicolour icons and solid stat cards tips into generic startup without the real product screens carrying the weight.

name: Plvs Ultra

type.note: Heavy over-tracked Poppins against very light Inter; 12px tracked caps in nav.

thesis: Makes an abstract pharma data engine tangible through one isometric hairline machine that dismantles itself as you scroll.
why_made: Every illustration shares the same isometric angle, stroke weight and single red signal, so the page reads as one drawn system. Red is reserved for the beam, buttons and data sparks.
watch_out: The -6px tracking collides letters at display size, and without a bespoke illustration set this is just dark Poppins with red pills.

name: Copilot

type.note: Navy #143352 instead of black, body at 70% of it; 11-13px JetBrains Mono for metadata such as reviewer names and plan tags.

thesis: Sells a finance assistant as soft and trustworthy, using navy type on luminous pastel fields with real UI floating on top.
why_made: Every panel holds a working fragment of the app with accurate data, tiny dollar glyphs and consistent 32px card radii. Motion is tied to the content: balances count, chart tags change, ratings roll.
watch_out: Pastel washes plus glossy blue pills is the most copied fintech look; without real UI fragments it turns into sugary template gradient.

name: Raycast Pricing

type.note: Slight positive tracking on dark for legibility. Prices are the largest type; the page has no hero headline at all.

thesis: Treats pricing as a native desktop app: near-black glass panels, physical-feeling keys and one streak of brand red.
why_made: A disciplined surface ladder from #07080A to #1E1F24, 1px white-alpha borders, and controls with real bevels make it feel machined. Density stays legible through two-tone rows and monospaced billing detail.
watch_out: Copying the bevels and glow without the tight surface ladder and 14px discipline yields muddy gaming-style dark UI.

name: reMarkable

type.note: Light custom serif with one italic word per headline; sturdy sans for body. Bold run-in lead-ins replace subheads.

thesis: Sells a tablet as calm stationery: paper tones, a light serif and offset editorial photo spreads instead of tech tropes.
why_made: Corners stay at 2px, one saturated blue sits on a paper-and-forest palette, and photography is graded to the page. Product UI is redrawn over handwriting so the interface feels printed rather than pasted.
watch_out: Without art-directed photography and a real display serif, square corners and big offsets look like an unfinished blog theme.

name: Sweetgreen

type.note: Extended grotesk with leading below font size; Grenette serif appears only for menu category tabs. Nav and item names in uppercase.

thesis: Lets one appetite-driven photo do the selling, then organises the page with oatmeal and sage panels split by hairlines.
why_made: Food photography is consistently lit and shot, and the custom wide type sets a strong voice. Acid lime is reserved for the top action, against deep green and oatmeal.
watch_out: The tight stacking of subheads under headlines and large empty tinted panels read as unfinished if the photography is not this strong.

name: Sailia

type.note: A tight-set book serif in a SaaS is the identity. Copy leading is too tight in places.

thesis: Gives booking software an outdoors spirit with cobalt fields, a tight book serif, marker strokes and sailing line art.
why_made: A single blue plus one fluorescent cyan stroke holds together photos, UI and drawings. Sections alternate cobalt and white and keep a square-cornered system.
watch_out: The marker underline on every heading gets repetitive, and the -3.4px serif tracking crowds letters.

name: Drizzle

type.note: System stack, no display type; 12px caps labels. Hierarchy comes from data rather than size.

thesis: A plain team index where live library stats, rendered as sparklines, are the whole design.
why_made: Modest and honest, it stays neat through a strict 3-column grid and repeated data structure. The usage trend in each card gives it credibility no marketing copy could.
watch_out: Without real data in the cards this is a bare bootstrap grid with an emoji.

name: Zed Pricing

type.note: Serif for headings and prices, quasi-mono for all body and UI, 11-13px caps mono labels; no size above 30px, so it reads like a well-set technical document.

thesis: Pricing as an engineering drawing: paper, hairline rails, one blue ink and keyboard shortcuts on every action.
why_made: The ruled frame runs through nav, content and footer, with diamond nodes at each junction. The page refuses large type and shadows, and small keyboard-native details prove it was designed by people who use the product.
watch_out: Rails and grids without a real content system become decoration; the texture must stay under ~5% contrast.

name: DixonBaxi

type.note: Semi-mono display face set small and centred; bold grotesk wordmark is the only other voice.

thesis: An agency homepage reduced to one prompt and one endless rail of work, with no nav and no scroll.
why_made: A 900px page with only a wordmark, a question and a precisely sprung card rail shows real confidence. Springy hover and measured 18px radii give the rail a tactile quality.
watch_out: Removing navigation only works when the work itself is outstanding; on an ordinary brief this reads as an empty page.

name: Razorpay Magic Checkout

type.note: Display face mixes Regular and SemiBold in a single line; white on sky and render backdrops, so contrast is thin in places.

thesis: Turns a checkout feature page into a 25,000px scroll film set on a floating island, with a phone changing state at each stop.
why_made: Pinned scenes hand off cleanly: one phone, one island and a shifting world tell a before and after, with real checkout UI embedded in 3D renders.
watch_out: Fantasy islands and glowing wireframes are a long way from a payments brand; the same treatment without strong 3D art looks like an AI-generated ad.

name: Supabase Pricing

type.note: Source Code Pro 46px/450 carries plan names and prices, so every number reads as data.

thesis: A usage-billed product made legible by treating pricing as a long spec sheet you keep scanning, not a marketing moment.
why_made: Mono prices against quiet Inter, one raised Pro column and a pinned plan header show real thought about reading a dense table.
watch_out: Copied without the hairline rhythm and group icons, forty rows of green buttons and checks become a spreadsheet dump.

name: Astral

type.note: H2 72px/75.6 and 48px/50.4 at -0.01em. Roboto Mono for timings and the 'built in the open' line.

thesis: A pixel-grid brand system where one stair-step shape drives the logo, hero glyph, panel corners and patterned patches.
why_made: Every surface obeys the same stepped grid and 12px radius, and acid lime is rationed against aubergine and sage. Measured type sizes and interlocking notches feel engineered, not decorated.
watch_out: Notches without a strict grid, or lime spread over large areas, turns it into a noisy retro gimmick.

name: Dogstudio

type.display: Didone logotype ~120px/105 for the slogan; Heebo 80px/60, 200 for project names
type.note: Capture shows an unsupported-browser banner on top; that strip is not part of the design.

thesis: An award-site showpiece where one WebGL creature is the whole interface and the work list orbits it.
why_made: The ultra-light 80px list against a heavy Didone slogan, plus one model recoloured per project, gives a clear single idea.
watch_out: Without a real art-directed model this is just a dark page with a slow 3D loader and unreadable grey text.

name: Liquid AI

type.note: Chakra Petch 11-13px tracked caps does all labelling, giving the serif a spec-sheet counterweight.

thesis: An AI lab that pairs a bookish serif with a ruled engineering grid to read as research first.
why_made: Hairline frame lines joining every section into cells, and a news rail where a hero image would normally be, make the page feel edited.
watch_out: Purple grain gradients and italic-purple emphasis are overused in AI; without the ruled frame it reverts to stock.

name: Noom

type.note: Pill buttons in BrownLL 14px/700 uppercase tracked; 80px/900 serif numerals for stats.

thesis: A mass-market consumer health funnel made calmer with a warm serif, tinted product cards and real people.
why_made: The retention-curve card and tinted product tiles explain the offer visually, with a consistent 20px radius and black pill system.
watch_out: The sticky promo card covers the hero headline; stacked bars, popups and back-to-top tabs quickly turn cheap.

name: Factory

type.note: Geist Mono uppercase 12-16px on every button and label is the voice of the page.

thesis: An enterprise AI tool dressed as precision industrial equipment: greyscale, square corners, mono labels, one orange dot.
why_made: A strict 24px gutter, 3px button radius and five-step neutral ladder hold across 9000px, and colour appears only as tiny orange dots and photographic grain. The restraint is total and the imagery does the warming.
watch_out: Copy the mono caps without the grainy imagery and exact grey ladder and it becomes an empty wireframe.

name: Framer

type.note: H2 44px/48.4, -1.76px. Input Mono only inside agent logs.

thesis: A true-black page that lets rebuilt product UI and customer sites supply all the colour.
why_made: Radii step cleanly from 20 to 15 to 8, borders are barely visible, and every demo is live DOM that fades out to black. The grid holds at 1200px while tight -4% headings keep it confident.
watch_out: Pure black with low-contrast UI fragments looks empty unless the fragments are real, dense and sharply rendered.

name: Paradigm

type.note: Custom pair. There is no headline: all copy is annotation size.

thesis: A venture firm's site as a five-slide instrument: live wireframe data sketches on blank paper, driven by keyboard.
why_made: 1px linework, tiny mono annotations and one pure green turn research into technical drawings. Each slide is a working visualisation, not an illustration.
watch_out: It explains nothing in the conventional sense; used for a normal product it is simply unusable.

name: Katja Ogrin

type.note: Almost everything is weight 600; hierarchy comes from size and grey only.

thesis: A live-events photographer's site on pure black where a few saturated frames do all the talking.
why_made: A two-colour UI, one type weight and a fixed 30px gutter stay out of the way, and the oversized monogram footer gives it a signature.
watch_out: Weak photography would collapse it instantly, and tight heavy Switzer at small sizes becomes dense.

name: Fly.io Docs

type.note: H2 25.5px/34 Mackinac 500. Fragment Mono for code; 1px purple link underlines.

thesis: Developer docs given a human voice through a warm serif and hand-inked spot illustrations.
why_made: The standard three-pane shell stays strict, so the watercolour art and bookish serif feel chosen rather than decorative.
watch_out: Generic clip art in this slot would look childish; it only works with one illustrator's consistent hand.

name: Lazy Eight

type.note: Largest text seen is ~14px on a 30,000px page. Measured 18px and 27px text does not appear in these frames.

thesis: A brand studio that replaces all selling with a 30,000px silent scroll of four-up image blocks.
why_made: A single repeated module, tiny type and huge voids give the work total authority, and the identical block format makes very different clients feel curated.
watch_out: Requires two dozen projects of equal photographic quality; with average imagery the emptiness just looks unfinished.

name: Sparklefilth

type.note: Novelty display face is spaced open and used for every heading and nav link; Inter carries the body so paragraphs stay readable.

thesis: A punk nerd-merch brand lets one pin-up mascot illustration and a dripping neon logo do all the work on a plain charcoal page.
why_made: The custom illustration is real commissioned-quality work, and the page stays disciplined around it: charcoal ground, one lavender family for surfaces, and neon saved for the art.
watch_out: Without bespoke illustration this becomes a clip-art page, and the novelty font fails at any size below ~14px.

name: Public

type.display: Denton Light, 80px/80, 300, normal tracking; 52px/57.72 for section heads
type.text: Inter 14-16px/~20 with Invest Pro for card titles
type.note: Serif only for statements. Hierarchy within a head comes from a second line in #a8b4bf, not from size.

thesis: A brokerage reads as a serious institution by pairing a light editorial serif with a very high density of real product UI on pure white and pure black.
why_made: Every feature shows redrawn working UI with true data states, and the system stays strict: 16px tray radius, hairlines, one teal accent, hard white-black cuts. Even the legal wall is typeset properly.
watch_out: The grey trays and faded UI crops turn generic fast if the UI inside is mocked with placeholder content rather than real states.

name: BIG

type.display: everett, 18px/20, 400, normal tracking is the largest size on the site
type.note: One family, sizes 12 to 18 only. There is no display type at all: the buildings supply the scale.

thesis: An architecture studio removes every interface convention and presents its whole body of work as one long single-file column of buildings.
why_made: Radical subtraction backed by a custom pictogram for each project: measured zero radii, zero shadows, zero bordered boxes, across ~790 images. The bespoke glyphs prove the restraint is designed, not unfinished.
watch_out: With weak or inconsistent imagery this is just an unstyled list, and the page only works if the photography carries everything.

name: 360Rides

type.note: Near-black heads over cool grey copy; green and coral each assigned to one audience.

thesis: A family ride app builds trust with soft mint and coral tints, warm parent-and-child photos and friendly 32px rounded surfaces.
why_made: The two-colour audience system (green for parents, coral for drivers) is held everywhere, and the 32px radius is consistent. The low-poly road hero gives a Framer template something ownable.
watch_out: 32px radii on everything plus pastel panels drifts into the stock Framer app template unless the imagery is specific.

name: PostHog Docs

type.note: 14px bold uppercase labels with .35px tracking; 10px tracked caps for volume metadata.

thesis: Docs are presented as a window on an illustrated desktop operating system, turning a reference index into a place with personality.
why_made: The OS metaphor is carried through precisely: menu bar, desktop icons, window controls and a dense but well-grouped index. Humour sits in the chrome while the content stays orderly.
watch_out: The desktop metaphor costs a lot of screen and is a one-brand move; copied elsewhere it is a costume, not a structure.

name: Jurafuchs

type.note: Coral eyebrow, bold head, grey sub: the same three-line stack opens nearly every section.

thesis: A German law-study app feels warm and approachable through soft peach neutrals, a rounded geometric sans and a sunset gradient borrowed from its logo.
why_made: Strong type choice and consistent section stacks, with evidence (study figures, ratings, press) placed high. Product UI is real and shown in restrained tinted panels.
watch_out: The gradient word plus rating chip plus avatar row is now a stock SaaS recipe; it needs a distinctive typeface to survive.

name: Vue

type.note: Ink is blue-grey #213547, not black, so the 900 weight stays friendly.

thesis: An open-source framework homepage acts as a calm signpost: one bold statement, a clear row of routes, then its sponsors.
why_made: Disciplined single-purpose layout with a well-judged slate ink and a single brand gradient word. It is plain, but the information order and small details are careful.
watch_out: The 900-weight centred headline with a gradient word is a dated default without the green brand equity behind it.

name: Stripe Sessions

type.note: Leading is below 1.0 at every display size; the ultralight weight is what makes it legible.

thesis: A conference page holds one extraordinary colour ribbon against an almost silent system of ultralight type, plum ink and hairlines.
why_made: Sub-1.0 leading on an ultralight grotesk, a strict one-third offset grid and plum in place of black. All colour is rationed to the ribbon, with only trace echoes in hover hairlines and day flags.
watch_out: Tight ultralight type fails on lesser fonts, and the page collapses without a render of this quality at its centre.

name: Synthesis

type.note: Slightly positive tracking on bold heads and nav gives a friendly, game-like voice.

thesis: A kids' maths tutor borrows the feel of a space game: deep night gradients, glowing tablet screens and a warm yellow call to action.
why_made: Real gameplay footage is the hero of nearly every section, and the background hue travels from royal blue to navy to maroon across the page. A single warm CTA stays visible throughout.
watch_out: Saturated gradients, bold type and gradient buttons together read as a mobile-game ad unless real product footage anchors them.

name: Definitiv Digital

type.text: Satoshi, 20px/30 at 80% white, key words bold white
type.note: Generous 1.3 leading on heads; one clause of each head is orange.

thesis: Software for trades businesses pairs a dark SaaS shell with real craftspeople and one reachable founder, so the product feels human.
why_made: The logo's chevron is promoted into a system of masks and tonal shapes, and the founder CTA gives the page a specific voice. Navy steps and orange are applied with discipline.
watch_out: Heavy repetition of the same avatar pill and orange clause gets salesy, and floating UI over cut-out portraits is easy to overcrowd.

name: Ideogram

type.text: Geist Variable, 16-18px/~26; Geist Mono for code
type.note: Serif only in the hero; all other sections are Geist, which reads cleaner but loses some character.

thesis: An image model sells itself by letting its own generated art fill the hero, then falling back to a calm white product page.
why_made: The WebGL liquid image swap is memorable, and the lavender is used as a real band of colour rather than a small accent. Below the hero the layout is orderly and well spaced.
watch_out: The page depends on the art direction of the generated images, and in this capture one logo image and one footer image render broken.

name: Patricia Ordoñez

type.note: No size above 20px; hierarchy comes from tracking, caps and colour blocks, not scale.

thesis: A whole CV compressed into one screen of pastel accordion blocks, reading like a tidy personal card rather than a portfolio.
why_made: The block gaps, radius and row heights are identical everywhere, and colour is confined to two flat panels. The restraint in type size makes it feel deliberate.
watch_out: Without strict 10px gaps and real copy, a stack of pastel bars turns into a link-in-bio template.

name: Kiro

type.text: AWS Diatype, 16px/23px; Fragment Mono for code
type.note: Rounded semi-mono display carries most of the brand; UI labels use uppercase mono.

thesis: A developer tool on pure black with one saturated violet and a ghost mascot, so an AWS product feels independent and friendly.
why_made: Real product UI appears at readable size inside large-radius panels, and violet is used in full-strength fields rather than thin accents.
watch_out: Copy the violet panels without the custom type and the real UI and it collapses into generic purple dark-mode SaaS.

name: Apple Intelligence

type.note: Almost one weight across the page; grey at weight 600 does the work other sites give to lighter text.

thesis: A long feature catalogue organised as bands of 28px-radius media cards, where the product screenshots supply all the colour.
why_made: Three radii, two surfaces and one heading style repeat for 12,000px without drift, and every caption obeys the same run-in rule. Depth comes only from overlap and ambient shadow on the hero collage.
watch_out: Without real, sharply art-directed screenshots the same layout becomes empty grey cards with big rounded corners.

name: Polar

type.text: PP Neue Montreal, 24px/33px for body, 16px for UI; GeistMono for token rows
type.note: Never bolder than 400 in headings. Hierarchy is white versus #858585 on the same size.

thesis: A billing product presented as a strict monochrome ledger: two-tone type, hairline rules and black product windows on grainy sand plates.
why_made: Colour is removed entirely, so spacing, a four-step neutral ladder and a single nested-window component carry every section. The one photographic texture is reused rather than varied, which reads as system, not decoration.
watch_out: Remove the sand plate and real tabular content and it becomes another empty black page with grey text.

name: Tailwind Docs

type.text: Inter, 16px/28px; IBM Plex Mono for labels and code
type.note: Mono is used for structure (group labels, step numbers), not only code.

thesis: Documentation treated as a drafting sheet, with hatched gutters and ruled cells framing a very calm reading column.
why_made: The double-framed code cards and hatch rails are small inventions on a standard docs layout, and they are applied with complete consistency.
watch_out: Hatching applied to more than the gutters turns a quiet frame into visual noise.

name: Sierra

type.note: Regular weight headlines only; tracking loosens as size falls.

thesis: Enterprise AI sold through tenderness: a sleeping baby instead of a dashboard, with the agent appearing as a quiet glass caption.
why_made: The emotional video and pale washed-out UI drawings keep it human, and the rounded white sheet lifting off the page gives a physical sense of layering.
watch_out: The four-colour gradient tiles are the weakest part and slip into stock AI bento if pushed further.

name: Postman

type.text: Inter, 16px; IBM Plex Mono 12-14px for labels and commands
type.note: Blacks and whites are warmed towards brown and cream, which sets it apart from neutral dark sites.

thesis: A warm brown-black developer page where a spectral horizon glow frames an install command, then settles into technical diagrams.
why_made: The warm-tinted neutrals and the gutter of contour line art give the dark theme its own identity. Diagrams and tables are drawn natively, not screenshotted.
watch_out: The rainbow horizon is one step from cliche AI glow if it spreads past the hero.

name: Storybook

type.note: Rounded humanist sans gives a community feel; it also dates the page slightly.

thesis: An open source tool's page built around its own app window, with a bright noisy gradient opening and scroll-spy section nav.
why_made: The product window is shown at full fidelity and the section nav turns a 15,000px page into something navigable.
watch_out: The many pastel tiles, brand colours and icon styles sit close to busy; add one more accent and it loses structure.

name: Exa

type.text: ABC Diatype, 15-17px/25px; GeistMono for data and labels
type.note: A warm text serif for voice, grotesque for UI, mono for numbers. Three families with strict roles.

thesis: A search API presented with the gravity of a research institute: warm serif headlines, hard-edged panels, and data in cobalt.
why_made: The serif is unexpected for AI infrastructure and every other element is squared off and technical, so the contrast feels authored. Cobalt appears only on data and the final footer, which makes both hit hard.
watch_out: The hard-cornered grid and stipple only work with real data behind them; with placeholder content they look like a bank template.

name: Airz Fitness

type.note: One condensed heavy caps face at very large size does nearly all the work.

thesis: A personal trainer site using huge condensed caps, one red and dark gym photography to feel physical.
why_made: The type scale commits fully and the red is used only on last words, tape and CTAs, so a small site feels confident despite stock-grade photos.
watch_out: The soft hero video and dated chrome logo pull it down; this approach needs sharp, real photography.

name: GitHub Pricing

type.text: Mona Sans, 16px/24px; Mona Sans Mono for labels
type.note: Fractional weights 440 and 460 keep the variable face from looking heavy at display size.

thesis: A pricing page drawn as a ruled ledger, with visible grid rails turning long plan data into a single continuous table.
why_made: Every element snaps to the same 1px rails, and the 16,000px comparison stays readable through a sticky header and one tinted check style.
watch_out: Remove the rails and strict alignment and it is just a very long table with green buttons.

name: Resend Docs

type.note: Monochrome: black is the only accent and links rely on underlines.

thesis: A docs shell where the article sits on a raised white sheet inside a grey app frame, so reading feels like a focused pane.
why_made: The inset sheet and restrained greys give a stock docs structure the feel of a native app, and the AI ask box is integrated rather than bolted on.
watch_out: The sheet effect depends on a very low-contrast grey; stronger shadows or tints make it look like a card template.

name: Hugging Face Pricing

type.note: IBM Plex Mono 14px sets all table data, the most-used face on the page by character count.

thesis: Turns a dense compute price list into an exposed engineering grid where rules and mono numerals do the work of decoration.
why_made: Visible page rails, dashed cells and mono tables give the long page one consistent logic. A single holographic button is the only indulgence, so it reads as special.
watch_out: Dashed lines everywhere plus heavy Source Sans can slide into a generic wireframe look if spacing rows are dropped.

name: TypeScript

type.display: Segoe UI, 40px, 200 with 600 for emphasis, normal
type.note: Cascadia Mono for code and for rotated margin notes; bold inline phrases carry skim-reading.

thesis: Explains a language by showing it working: real editor errors and annotated code do the selling on a flat brand-blue and white page.
why_made: The teaching devices are thought through, especially hand-noted code and step bars that show gradual adoption. Square corners and thin rules keep it honest, though parts feel dated.
watch_out: Square black outlines and default blue links read as an old corporate site once the code content is removed.

name: Analogue

type.note: One family and two weights; size alone sets hierarchy. Fluid scale lands on values like 52.89px and 17.63px.

thesis: Runs a retro-gaming hardware store like a gallery: one render, one sentence and one black pill per full-bleed block.
why_made: Renders share the page's exact ground, so products sit in the layout instead of on top of it. Nav, footer and base row all reuse one set of column positions, with two radii and zero shadows across the page.
watch_out: With stock or mid-quality renders the formula collapses, because nothing else on the page carries interest.

name: Loopcraft

type.note: Tight Jakarta display over quiet Inter; card titles pick up each product's own colour.

thesis: A warm Maldivian studio site built around big tight sans statements and a sticky stack of its own products.
why_made: The word-fill manifesto and the app-icon rail are strong scroll ideas, and the capsule nav stays calm over everything. Polish thins out in the service cards and the hero's legibility.
watch_out: White headline on a busy office photo is hard to read, and a sparkle emoji beside a heading cheapens it quickly.

name: Auth0

type.note: Aeonik Mono in tracked caps labels data and stats; regular-weight display lets the gradient stay loud while type stays calm.

thesis: Gives identity infrastructure a dramatic sunset-on-plum brand field with hairline cell layouts and mono labels underneath.
why_made: Rigid 1px cell grids and a square 4px radius discipline the saturated gradient. The journey dial and pinned feature index are real interaction ideas, not stock sections.
watch_out: The purple-to-coral field is close to a dark-mode SaaS cliche, and the capture's persistent chat widget shows how quickly it gets crowded.

name: Discord

type.note: Ultra-wide black caps with tight stacked leading; friendly humanist text keeps paragraphs readable.

thesis: A loud, playful brand world of 3D characters, starfields and giant bubble panels that sells hanging out rather than software.
why_made: A custom extended typeface and consistent character set hold the noise together, while real product UI stays crisp inside soft panels. Details like the collapsing nav and footer gag show real care.
watch_out: Without the custom type and character art this becomes a garish purple gradient page with oversized rounded boxes.

name: Hugging Face Docs

type.note: A deliberately small scale: nothing above 24px, so the page reads as an index, not marketing.

thesis: A docs landing page that behaves like a well-ruled table of contents rather than a hero with cards.
why_made: Everything shares one dashed grid, and tiny colour squares give scanning cues without icons. Density comes from restraint in size rather than from clutter.
watch_out: Without the exact small type and the spacer rows it reads as an unstyled link list.

name: Forma24

type.note: Montserrat 38px/400 at -1.9px for section heads, Geist Mono 12px caps for tags. Three families is one too many.

thesis: A near-black agency page that uses mono tags, hairline tables and a founder booking card to look more like a product than a studio.
why_made: The comparison table and case-study cards are properly structured, and the booking card turns the CTA into a person. Consistent mono labelling holds the sections together.
watch_out: AI-looking office photos and tight Montserrat tracking are what make this feel like a premium template rather than a studio's own work.

name: Biome

type.note: JetBrains Mono for tabs, code and terminal; fairly generous tracking on the headline for Geist.

thesis: A docs-theme landing page that proves itself with real code and benchmark panels instead of marketing surfaces.
why_made: The three-pane formatter proof and package-manager tabs are real working evidence presented cleanly. The rest stays calm with hairline panels and soft corner washes.
watch_out: A crowded nav and a repeated logo lockup already flirt with a default docs template, so copied loosely it looks unfinished.

name: mymind

type.note: Serif owns every big statement at 140/96/54px, Inter sets feature titles at 40px/500, Nunito handles pills, tags, nav and caps labels.

thesis: Sells a calm private memory tool through oversized bookish serif type, a soft sunset glow and interface props that behave like physical objects.
why_made: Each demo is art-directed with specific human content rather than lorem or fake dashboards, and the tag pill recurs from sentence to nav to AI labels. Colour stays in soft fields and one orange, so the page feels warm instead of busy.
watch_out: Blurred rainbow glows plus a big serif turn into generic wellness-app styling without the art direction and object-quality demos.

name: Soundsensing

type.note: Moderat carries everything; Geist Mono 12px appears only on data labels such as SYSTEM STATUS and UP TO.

thesis: Makes industrial HVAC sensing feel premium by pairing grainy macro photography of real equipment with sparse frosted status UI and a cool sage palette.
why_made: Real installed hardware replaces stock imagery, and a sage-to-stone colour pair runs through type, cards and buttons. Small 4-8px radii, equal-weight buttons and sentence headings keep it sober.
watch_out: Without the macro photo and film grain, the small radii and muted sage become a plain corporate template.

name: Nicole Heim Studio

type.text: Arno Pro SmText, 20px/25px; Universal Sans Text 15px/500 for labels; Apercu Mono 15px for captions
type.note: Three sizes only (63, 20, 15). No bold, no accent colour, and mono appears only on caption detail lines.

thesis: A fashion brand studio that behaves like a lookbook: split-screen editorial photography interrupted by oversized serif statements, with almost no interface.
why_made: One 32px margin and three type sizes govern the whole page, and the serif is a true display cut set tight. Art-directed photography does all the colour work, so the UI never needs an accent.
watch_out: Without real art direction and a licensed optical serif, the emptiness collapses into a stock portfolio template.

name: 1X

type.text: ABC Diatype, 14px; nav and footer 10-12px caps with ~+1.5px tracking
type.note: One display size on the whole site; every section is one 44px line split into two tones.

thesis: A robotics company presented as a quiet fashion campaign: three soft-knit robots on warm grey, then full-screen scenes carrying one line each.
why_made: Every screen holds one two-tone 44px line, one action and nothing else, pinned to the same margins across hero, careers and film. The tiny tracked caps nav and the render dissolving into the ground feel expensive.
watch_out: This only works with a bespoke image; on stock renders one small line reads as an unfinished page, and the dark nav already vanishes over the dusk photos.

name: Devin Desktop (codeium.com redirect)

type.text: NB International Pro ~17px/22px for copy; Inter 13-15px inside UI; IBM Plex Mono 12px for metadata
type.note: codeium.com now redirects to devin.ai/desktop; this card grades that page. All headings are weight 400, and hierarchy comes from grey versus black.

thesis: A desktop agent app sold by its own interface: rebuilt UI fragments on painterly image plates, held inside a ruled page frame with quiet two-tone type.
why_made: Every screenshot is a legible HTML rebuild sitting on a soft photographic plate, so the page feels like the product. Rails, hairlines and one regular-weight headline voice make a strict, calm ledger.
watch_out: The calm depends on real, specific UI content; with lorem rows or a generic gradient plate it becomes default SaaS.

name: lemon.markets

type.display: Neue Haas Grotesk Display Pro, 56px/72px, 400, tight by default
type.text: General Sans, 16-18px/28px; ui-monospace 12px in code panels
type.note: Display leading of 1.3 is loose for the size and gives the page its unhurried, documentation-like feel.

thesis: A brokerage API explained through isometric line drawings, with one lemon yellow as the only colour across alternating near-white and ink bands.
why_made: A tiny illustration kit of ink outlines, flat yellow faces and solid ellipse shadows carries every section, and the doubled offset card outline recurs across logos, lists and panels.
watch_out: Isometric line art turns to clip art without strict stroke weight and one accent; the hero sphere here already collides with the body copy.

name: SC Program

type.text: Inter, 15-16px/~20px; JetBrains Mono 11-12px caps for labels; Caveat for handwritten notes
type.note: -6% tracking is extreme and only survives at display size.

thesis: A direct-response video sales letter dressed in dark product-launch styling, where every block pushes to one full-width blue button.
why_made: Funnel mechanics are built with product-grade parts: consistent 12px radii, mono micro labels, rebuilt course UI and a single blue. That polish makes a hard sell read as considered.
watch_out: Glow frames, income claims, handwritten notes and walls of chat screenshots read as get-rich-quick the moment they leave this exact brief.

name: Fairphone

type.note: Bricolage is reserved for headings and prices in deep green; DM Sans carries everything else.

thesis: A sustainable electronics shop where big rounded product panels and deep green with acid lime make repairability feel desirable rather than worthy.
why_made: Radii are deliberately mixed, 40px soft panels against 0-radius outlined buttons, and the inktrap grotesque adds warmth. Product imagery stays on neutral ground throughout.
watch_out: Stack a region popup, chat bubble and accessibility button over rounded cards and the page crowds quickly; keep overlays out of the product frame.

name: Tally

type.note: Serif asterisk wordmark is the only break from Inter; hand-drawn marks supply the personality the type does not.

thesis: A free form builder that feels like a Notion doc with someone doodling in the margins: plain Inter on white, ink drawings and one magenta marker.
why_made: Illustration comes from one hand and pen weight across the page, and magenta is rationed to icons, underlines and scribbles. Product panels look live and type themselves.
watch_out: Doodles without one illustrator's hand read as clip art; keep them in the margins and never behind text.

name: Foster + Partners

type.note: Custom logotype with hairline plus carries identity; headings stay deliberately modest.

thesis: An architecture practice's home page as a dark image index: one cinematic film, then a strict grid of captioned photographs and quote panels.
why_made: The grid is rigid at 24px gaps and two-thirds plus one-third rows, and #1a1a1a lets photographs glow. Small captions and no CTAs trust the work.
watch_out: Open Sans and a heavy gradient on every tile feel early-2010s, so only top-class photography rescues it.

name: Boston Dynamics

type.note: Generous 1.65 body leading softens a heavy geometric headline voice.

thesis: An industrial robotics company using studio-lit robot portraits on deep blue gradient bands to turn heavy machinery into a friendly product line.
why_made: Robots are shot as hero products under controlled blue and yellow light, and one grainy blue gradient ties bands to photography. Gotham Bold gives a confident engineering voice.
watch_out: Noise-gradient bands plus tall Gotham lean corporate, and the desktop hero captured as a white void because its media loads late.

name: Docker

type.note: Repro's wide geometric shapes appear only on headings.

thesis: A legacy developer brand reframed for agents: a boxed, ruled page with a black glyph-field hero and real terminal panels in blue-tinted whites.
why_made: A 1160px boxed frame with side hairlines gives structure, and terminals hold believable output. A blue fade at the base of cards ties the palette together.
watch_out: Boxed frames with side rails look dated unless the outer margins are deliberate, and the blue-fade card is easy to overuse.

name: Fujifilm X

type.text: Noto Sans, 14-18px; Noto Sans JP for fallback
type.note: The measured 112px line height on 30px titles is a layout device for spacing inside tiles, not reading leading.

thesis: A camera brand home page built as an edge-to-edge contact sheet of photographers shooting with the product, with condensed captions over darkened images.
why_made: Zero-gap tiles on strict half and quarter splits, and every frame shows hands on a real camera, so the page reads as one shoot.
watch_out: The uniform ~30% black overlay dulls the photos and Fjalla One shows its free-font limits; protect text with a local gradient instead of flattening the image.

name: Svix

type.text: Neue Haas, 16px/24px with tight tracking; GeistMono 12-16px for labels, links and footer
type.note: Tight tracking is applied at all sizes, including body, which is where it goes too far.

thesis: Infrastructure sold as precision hardware: chrome hex nuts and machined plates on cool grey, with hexagons and screw heads as the system's signature.
why_made: The hexagon runs through logo, renders, icons, bullets and rules, and feature cards hold bespoke mini UIs rather than screenshots. The logo grid's broken lines and corner ticks show rare attention.
watch_out: Screws and chrome on every panel tip into gimmick, and -4% tracking on body text hurts reading.

name: Bun

type.display: Archivo condensed, ~72px hero to 117px/100.6px closing band, 900, -1.17px
type.note: Martian Mono 11-13px does every label, command and number, so three voices have strict jobs: slab headline, grey prose, mono data.

thesis: A runtime homepage built like a lab report, where every section proves a claim with a benchmark, a real terminal or a real command.
why_made: One condensed black face, one mono and one hot pink sit in a hairline-ruled 1136px column. The clipped corner on every button and code block turns a plain box system into something owned.
watch_out: Hard boxes and mono labels become brutalist cosplay if the data is invented or the hairlines and spacing drift.

name: Sidekick

type.note: The real display face is the custom block wordmark; DM Sans at -6% tracking only has to stay out of its way.

thesis: A coordination agency reduced to one slit-cut square: the logo is the hero, the scroll object and the footer.
why_made: Three colours, one typeface and one shape run the entire page. The slit motif comes from the wordmark's own letter construction, so every graphic feels drawn by the same hand.
watch_out: A wordmark this heavy only works if it is genuinely custom; a chunky display font stretched across the top looks like a template.

name: Stripe Atlas

type.note: H2s are 38px/48px -0.2px. The scale has only five working sizes: 56, 38, 18, 15, 13.

thesis: A legal product sold as calm software, with the incorporation flow itself as hero on a ruled page crossed by one slanted orange band.
why_made: A visible four-column grid governs every block, type holds a strict scale, and one hue drives links, eyebrows, ticks and the gradient. Dense legal content ends up feeling light.
watch_out: The slanted gradient without real UI and a strict grid is a generic 2018 startup page.

name: Symbol Studio

type.note: Caps headings at 40-72px alternate with 22px sentence case; 11-12px caps handle every caption.

thesis: A branding studio presented as one strict white sheet inset on pale grey, held by a black segmented nav and a single orange.
why_made: The 16px inset frame, centre hairline, one grotesque and uniform 8-10px radii make very different sections feel like pages of one document.
watch_out: Without real client marks and consistent photography, boxed caps headings go flat and corporate.

name: ClickHouse

type.note: Section heads are basier at 36px; numerals are Inter 700 at 72px.

thesis: A database homepage that spends all its colour on one acid yellow, stepping between charcoal sections and flat yellow cards and bands.
why_made: Yellow appears at three fixed scales (button, card, band) on a stepped charcoal ladder, and framed line icons keep dense content organised.
watch_out: Stacking too many yellow blocks under centred headings becomes loud and repetitive; the charcoal rests are what make it work.

name: Spotify

type.note: Application scale: nothing above 24px, hierarchy comes from weight and #fff versus #b3b3b3.

thesis: The logged-out web player, a three-panel music app where cover art supplies all the colour and the chrome stays black.
why_made: Panels share one radius and gap on a black shell, type stays small and strict, and shape does semantic work: square for releases, circle for people.
watch_out: Panel layouts collapse badly on small screens; this capture clips the main panel on phones, and the shell needs real content density to not feel empty.

name: PostHog Handbook

type.note: Display is small because the window is the composition; size never needs to shout.

thesis: A company handbook staged as a toy desktop operating system, with windows, icons and a hedgehog mascot in place of a docs site.
why_made: The metaphor is carried through every part: menu bar, icons, window controls, even the joke cookie card. Sage tints are mixed from the grass wallpaper, so the whole screen sits in one palette.
watch_out: An OS metaphor without this much illustration and copy discipline is a gimmick that makes content harder to find.

name: Freshly Launched

type.display: PP Neue Montreal plus PP Editorial New Thin Italic, 72px/72px, 100, -0.72px
type.note: Serif thin italic is used for one phrase per heading; the condensed upright Editorial handles quotes and captions.

thesis: A Shopify and email studio that sells taste through its own art-directed still life and client work rather than through claims.
why_made: Warm photographs set the palette and the type pair is applied consistently, with one thin italic phrase per heading.
watch_out: Thin italic serif over a busy photo loses legibility fast, and this pairing is a very common Framer look without original imagery.

name: Nx

type.note: Fragment Mono 12px for commands; large figures such as '9.2x faster' use Inter 68px/64.6px -2.38px.

thesis: A near-black monorepo page that keeps flipping to white isometric panels, turning the abstract idea of caching into physical objects.
why_made: One isometric drawing language and one electric-blue cube explain every concept, and thin connector lines tie the customer boxes into a single diagram.
watch_out: Near-black plus grey copy plus a blue glow is the default dev-tool page; without the custom diagrams nothing here is distinctive.

name: Bonobos

type.note: Spezia Serif at 48px gives editorial section heads; a mono appears only in the promo modal.

thesis: A menswear store that mixes campaign video with a three-voice type system of narrow caps, serif headings and quiet sans.
why_made: The narrow caps, serif and tracked caps labels each hold a fixed job across hero, shelves and tiles, and the olive ground ties photography together.
watch_out: Judged from load and phone frames, since a promo modal covers every desktop stop; stacked modals, chat bubbles and accessibility widgets quickly bury this restraint.

name: Stability AI

type.note: Second clauses tint to grey, lilac or plum; 42px section heads repeat the two-tone trick.

thesis: A generative media company showing its output as cinema, with charcoal and blush sections framing large videos and one lilac.
why_made: Lilac is pulled from the hero footage and used across buttons, tints and stat glass, so generated imagery and interface share a palette.
watch_out: Glass UI fragments and dashed connectors over video turn messy fast, and here they collide with the nav.

name: Notion Calendar

type.note: H2 42px/48px -1.5px. Lyon Text appears once, for the footer quote.

thesis: A calendar page as plain as Notion itself: black type, warm grey panels and real UI, with small coloured event stickers supplying all the play.
why_made: A strict 1024px column, one warm grey, one radius and three type sizes keep dense screenshots calm. The floating stickers reuse the app's event chip, so colour comes from the product's own vocabulary.
watch_out: Floating icons become clip-art confetti unless they share one line style and stay out in the margins.

name: Charles Pas

type.note: One size on the whole site; only black versus light grey separates current from secondary.

thesis: An artist's site as a single framed photograph, with oversized bold text around it and a name that bends across the picture when you scroll.
why_made: One photograph, one typeface, one size. The bold 35px text is large enough to act as image, and the white frame is exact on all sides.
watch_out: This only works with a strong photograph and real authorship; used for a normal business it reads as an empty page.

name: Adrien Quéchon 2026 Website

type.note: Serif display against mono HUD micro-labels

thesis: A developer portfolio dressed as a monochrome terminal HUD with a WebGL smoke backdrop and editorial serif statements.
why_made: Strict two-font system and a consistent grey radial vignette make every mono label feel like instrumentation; the loader and scroll are choreographed as one piece.
watch_out: Tiny mono text at low contrast on grey becomes unreadable and the HUD gimmick collapses without the WebGL atmosphere.

name: Design Podcast (Focus State)

type.display: PP Editorial New, 64px/1.1, 400, -0.02em (logo is pixel serif ~220px)
type.text: PP Editorial New 12-20px; PP Mondwest for pixel accents
type.note: Serif body at small size with hairline-ruled metadata

thesis: A podcast index where each episode is a split-screen of duotone photo plus gradient-filled circles, all on a strict half-and-half grid.
why_made: One repeated module (photo, circle motif, ruled metadata) with a different hue per episode gives variety with total system discipline.
watch_out: Saturated duotones and gradient circles turn garish without the strict black/white frame and tiny restrained serif text.

name: Curology

type.note: Serif Caslon-style accent in the collab title

thesis: A telehealth skincare brand using full-bleed campaign photography and a single violet pill CTA over a clean white commerce layout.
why_made: Real skin, unretouched faces and consistent violet accent make a medical product feel human; product carousels are tidy and evenly spaced.
watch_out: Violet CTA repeated every section and stacked carousels can read as generic DTC if photography is stock.

name: A24

type.display: Neue Montreal, 400px hero titles, weight 485, -0.05em, lh 0.8
type.note: Oversized film titles bleed off the frame

thesis: A film studio site that lets full-bleed stills and oversized white titles carry each release, with a white catalogue below.
why_made: Huge tight-leaded titles over cinematic frames, then a calm white index with hairlines: extreme scale contrast with disciplined small type.
watch_out: 400px titles with negative tracking need strong photography and a dark scrim; on weak images they just collide with faces.

name: Julia Loyd Mohr

type.display: Editorial Old Ultralight, 70px/1.05, 400, italic for second line
type.text: Apercu Mono 11-12px, blue accent for tags
type.note: Light italic serif against mono tags

thesis: A branding designer's portfolio with a fixed olive half-screen introduction beside a scrolling cream column of project plates.
why_made: The permanent olive panel anchors the brand while diverse client work scrolls past in uniform plates, so identity and portfolio stay coherent.
watch_out: Ultralight serif at 70px needs the dark olive field; on a lighter ground it would vanish.

name: Eicher Honig

type.note: Serif headings with grotesk body

thesis: A regional honey producer using gingham-yellow brand cues, real beekeeper photography and plain honest information.
why_made: The gingham lid pattern is lifted from the jar label into the header, so brand and product are one; photography is authentic and warm.
watch_out: Heavy yellow bars plus default-sized body copy can look like a template if the photography is not this authentic.

name: Locomotive

type.note: Custom serif with glyph-ligature icons embedded in text

thesis: An agency site as a typeset document: hairline-ruled lists of serif names on white with black cut-out video figures.
why_made: Consistent 1px rules, one custom serif and tiny grotesk labels give a gallery-catalogue precision; surprise comes from cut-out 3D people and inline pictograms.
watch_out: Without a custom typeface and the hairline grid, centered serif lists look like a Word document.

name: Salterra Resort & Spa

type.note: Mixed upright and italic terracotta words in headings

thesis: A Caribbean resort in terracotta and sand with soft textured panels and hospitality-standard booking chrome.
why_made: A tight palette of terracotta and cream plus grainy blush textures gives a calm, expensive resort tone; the booking affordances are always present.
watch_out: Pale type on cream and small light-weight labels fall below readable contrast; image placeholders in this capture show the page depends on photography.

name: DOT Audio Recorder

type.note: Section heads 40-45px

thesis: A Mac utility pitched with a warm sunset gradient hero, dark rounded cards and one red CTA.
