thesis: A furniture maker's home page run like an honest catalogue: Univers, one link colour and photographs of real homes.
why_made: Extreme restraint in type sizes plus strict column alignment carries the Dieter Rams ethos, and the copy is as calm and specific as the layout.
watch_out: With stock photos or a lesser grotesque the same layout reads as a 2012 corporate CMS.

name: Cal.com

type.note: Section heads 56px, 24px muted leads, all one family. The face is cut so tight it reads far tighter than the measured -0.8px. ui-monospace only for code.

thesis: A scheduling product sold by showing real UI fragments in one grey-on-white tile system, warmed by dithered documentary photos.
why_made: One tile recipe of hairline shell, 8px inset and #f3f4f8 well repeats for every feature, and what sits inside is real component UI. Halftoned photography gives an ownable texture that carries through to the footer wordmark.
watch_out: Headline chips and double-rim cards turn cheap fast when the chips are decorative or the radii do not nest.

name: Payload

type.note: GeistMono only for the install command. Footer heads 12px uppercase with wide tracking; 48px dimmed list as a scroll device.

thesis: A CMS framework presented as an engineering drawing, with visible page grid lines over black and one filmic streak of colour.
why_made: Every block hangs from five visible vertical rules, so the grid itself is the ornament, and the colour field appears only around the hero with a dot-screen grain.
watch_out: Grid lines running through body copy hurt legibility, and empty cells look unfinished if content does not snap to them.

name: React Email

type.note: CommitMono for code, chips and install commands. Headline carries a light-to-grey vertical fill. Section heads ~35px, 500.

thesis: An email component library whose hero wraps real email templates into glowing ribbons around a dark void.
why_made: The ribbon makes the product itself the hero image, and everything else stays dim so it alone owns colour. Tiles use faint top-edge highlights instead of shadows.
watch_out: Grey-on-near-black sections with large gaps feel empty; without the hero object this is generic dark mode.

name: Rewiring America

type.note: Friendly serif headlines over grotesque body. 14px bold uppercase labels. Secondary colours coral, aqua and lilac appear only inside illustrations.

thesis: A climate nonprofit makes electrification feel warm and optimistic with sunshine yellow, serif headlines and wiring that literally connects the page.
why_made: The wire motif runs from logo to connector lines to footer outline, so the page has one idea. Illustrations and photos share a defined palette of coral, aqua and lilac.
watch_out: Full yellow plus friendly serif goes childish without custom illustration and the wire motif.

name: MotherDuck

type.note: Aeonik Mono and JetBrains Mono for labels and terminals. Positive tracking on all-caps display is the signature.

thesis: A serverless database sold through a cartoon sky of ducks and clouds laid over rigorously boxed architecture diagrams.
why_made: Hard outlines and solid offset shadows make every box look printed, uppercase mono keeps the humour technical, and the diagrams explain the real product.
watch_out: Outline-plus-mascot neo-brutalism becomes childish when every section shouts or the diagrams are empty decoration.

name: Baseten

type.note: Geist Mono 12px uppercase for every label. Section heads 56px/61.6px, -1.12px. One regular weight carries all display type.

thesis: Inference infrastructure drawn as an isometric pixel city on a severe square grid, with a black-and-white base and one colour per product.
why_made: Nothing has a radius, one weight carries all display type, and mono labels sit in bars cut to exact grid columns. Dotted seams replace section dividers and the world recolours per product.
watch_out: Without the real isometric scene and exact column snapping, the square tiles and dotted bands read as a brutalist template.

name: a16z

type.display: Custom Art Deco gold lettering as artwork, ~56px cap height, wide letter spacing
type.note: DOM text is only 11 and 14px; Domaine serif and Domaine Sans sit under a slogan that is an image.

thesis: A venture firm's home page reduced to one 900px screen: a cinematic film reel, a gold Art Deco slogan and no scroll.
why_made: The film is graded consistently dark with a vignette that keeps overlays legible, and all UI stays quiet in a thin frame around it.
watch_out: Without a real film budget this is just a video background, and it offers no information hierarchy.

name: Polestar

type.note: Only four sizes exist: 12, 16, 30, 110px, in one weight. Leading is very tight even on body. No colour accent at all; photography supplies it.

thesis: A car brand presented as a Swiss catalogue: one grotesque, four sizes, square outlines and large quiet photography doing the selling.
why_made: Four type sizes, one weight, zero button radii and a 6-column grid make heavy promotional and legal content feel composed. Even footnotes are set on the grid.
watch_out: Tight 16/18 body and -4.5% display tracking need a tuned grotesque; in a default sans it looks cramped rather than confident.

name: Rspack

type.note: Scale steps 72/50/48; Menlo 12px for benchmark values only. Default docs-theme type, no custom face.

thesis: A friendly open-source bundler homepage built on a docs theme, given character by a crab mascot and an orange speed gradient.
why_made: The benchmark bars make the whole pitch in one graphic, and the red-to-orange gradient runs consistently from wordmark to data fills to corner brackets.
watch_out: Default Open Sans and gradient text sit close to a stock docs template, so the mascot and real benchmarks must do all the differentiating.

name: Russell & Stellar

type.display: Canela Bold Italic, measured 127px, renders ~88px/1.0, 700, normal, uppercase
type.note: Lora 24-44px carries headings, buttons and eyebrows; Canela is reserved for the hero and one VIEW ALL overlay.

thesis: A spirits consultancy styled like a Riviera drinks ad, with sun-drenched photography, a bold italic serif and a bespoke martini mark.
why_made: Photography is art-directed for warmth and saturation, and the hero type with its martini glyph reads as a brand lockup rather than a heading. Cream, navy and a late acid yellow keep the palette ownable.
watch_out: The loose offsets and big gaps depend on striking photos, and the team map shows how quickly the concept tips into clip-art.

name: Amplitude

type.note: Measured family reads Twemoji Country Flags, which is a font-stack artefact; rendered face is Gellix. H2s 56/62 and 44/48 at -0.5px. IBM Plex Sans inside product UI.

thesis: An analytics platform reframed as an AI product, led by real app states on a white page paced by hairlines, with no decorative gradients.
why_made: One geometric typeface at a few tight sizes, black pills and inset hairlines do all the structural work, while auto-advancing product tabs and a single-series chart carry the proof. The full-width footer wordmark gives a calm page one loud ending.
watch_out: White-and-hairline pages go blank without high-fidelity product states, and the emoji chat widget here shows how fast a third-party bubble undercuts the restraint.

name: Mirim

type.note: H2s 60/66. Chivo Mono 12-16px uppercase for nav, TOC title, labels and step names. Body leading is unusually tight.

thesis: A studio case study told as a guided read, with a sticky contents rail and a logo-derived column motif carrying plum, cream and orange throughout.
why_made: The stepped columns from the logo recur as hero watermark, blue panel shapes and orange CTA field, and Chivo Mono labels give each section the same dry voice. The pinned process timeline shows real choreography.
watch_out: Tight body leading and a large AI assistant panel crowding the first screen show how quickly a dense case study turns cluttered.

name: Upstash

type.note: Second display size 180/225 for the Fast Anywhere gradient H2; H2s 48/48 600; JetBrains Mono in code panels.

thesis: A serverless data platform in mint on grey, with huge gradient type and product-tab panels leading straight to copyable code.
why_made: Large-radius white blocks on soft mint fields and dark code panels create depth without borders, and the agent-prompt CTA is a sharp, current touch.
watch_out: Gradient headline text, r35 cards and coloured pills are the familiar SaaS kit, so they look cheap once product and code content thin out.

name: Neon Docs

type.note: H2s 26/32.5 at -1.04px, so all headings track -0.04em. GeistMono 12-14px for product labels and prompts.

thesis: A docs home run like a terminal-tinted index: square hairline cards, mono labels and a left rail, with an agent prompt as the first action.
why_made: A strict near-zero-radius grid, tight -0.04em Inter headings and green reserved for capability cards give a dense page clear order. Black pills are the only round shapes, so the action is always obvious.
watch_out: Square mint boxes with mono labels look like a wireframe if spacing drifts or green spreads beyond the capability cards.

name: Brilliant

type.note: Serif for H1 and chapter heads (54, 44); CoFo Brilliant sans 30/38 for feature heads. Italic only on subject words. Link teal #279b8d.

thesis: A tutoring product sold by showing real interactive lessons, with a warm serif voice on a calm paper-toned page.
why_made: The fan of genuine problem cards and cropped lesson UI do the selling, while a few tokens (sand, white, black, one green) hold steady for 8,000px. Tactile button edges and a blur-through capsule nav are the only flourishes.
watch_out: Serif-plus-italic on sand becomes generic wellness styling if product imagery is stock or placeholder rather than real lesson UI.

name: Globe Limousines

type.display: Söhne Kräftig, measured 24px/28.8px, renders ~30px/36px, 500, normal, uppercase
type.note: Söhne Buch for buttons; small serif eyebrows in champagne. No display scale above ~30px.

thesis: A Geneva limousine firm presented through aerial city video and a strict charcoal palette with a single champagne accent.
why_made: Consistent concrete-studio car shots and small disciplined uppercase Söhne feel corporate-luxe rather than flashy, and frosted overlapping panels add depth to a neutral ladder.
watch_out: With no large type and long centred copy it turns monotonous, and gold on charcoal becomes limo cliché if photography slips.

name: Peloton

type.note: Not the fitness brand: this is oil and gas data software. H2s 46/42.3 at -1.38px; Univers caps with tracking for nav and buttons.

thesis: Industrial oil-and-gas data software rendered as dark navy signage, with condensed caps and one field-equipment green.
why_made: Condensed two-tone headings give a text-heavy B2B page a strong, sector-appropriate voice, and the steel navy ladder with coded card edges keeps many products organised.
watch_out: Dot-wave backdrops, Venn spheres and boxed-everything date quickly, and without the strict type rule this density reads like a 2018 enterprise theme.

name: Basic Agency

type.note: Measured maximum is only 22/24.2 at -0.77px; large statements were not captured in the DOM sample, so display size is estimated from frames.

thesis: An agency site that behaves like a reel, with hard-cut client footage, shouted caps statements and a page whose colour flips as you scroll.
why_made: One grotesk at extreme scale contrast, print-like grain and a single pink accent hold together client work of any colour. The cursor discs, theme inversion and rules feel authored rather than plugged in.
watch_out: All-caps statements and cursor tricks read as try-hard without very strong footage and tight tracking at display sizes.

name: Webflow Pricing

type.note: One variable family throughout, steps 80/56/32/24/20/16.

thesis: A pricing page built as a dense reference table, kept usable by a sticky billing toggle, collapsible plan families and strict hairlines.
why_made: Fused plan columns, consistent 51px blue buttons and tight price numerals make complex tiers scannable, and grainy light-band panels give the grey rigour one atmospheric relief.
watch_out: Copying the density without the sticky toggle, collapsed sections and exact alignment gives an unreadable wall of blue buttons.

name: Jasper

type.note: Scale 14/16/18/32/48/64/88. Feature serif owns headings and numerals, ABC ROM owns everything read at length; no third family.

thesis: An enterprise AI platform dressed as a confident print identity: tight serif, square boxes and flat geometric colour instead of the usual gradient tech look.
why_made: One rule runs everywhere: 1px navy boxes with zero radius, flat fills only, and grid-paper and circle motifs that recur from hero to FAQ. Five flat colours each have a fixed job.
watch_out: Hairline square boxes read as a wireframe unless the serif is this tight and the colour blocks this confident.

name: web.dev

type.note: Roboto and Material Icons only in utility chrome. Sizes 12/14/16/20/32/48/64.

thesis: A documentation front door that treats learning topics as an orderly catalogue, with one illustration language doing all the warmth.
why_made: Strict alternation of white and tinted bands, a single outline-pill button and a consistent illustration set keep a large content hub calm and scannable.
watch_out: Without the illustrations this is default Material layout; copying only the structure gives a bland corporate docs page.

name: Xin Cheng Foods

type.note: Wide positive tracking on heavy CJK headings; 1.5 leading gives each line of Hanzi room.

thesis: A family biscuit manufacturer turns its product's scalloped edge into the site's whole shape language.
why_made: Scalloped edges, biscuit-shaped cards and dome panels all derive from the product, and the indigo and cream come straight from the packaging shown in the real studio photographs.
watch_out: Wavy dividers become stock clip-art the moment they are not tied to the product and matched to real photography.

name: MetaLab

type.note: Only three sizes on the page: 12, 16, 88. All interface text is grotesque, the one serif line is the statement.

thesis: An agency homepage reduced to one sentence, a client list and a looping liquid object, with the load sequence doing the persuading.
why_made: Extreme economy: three type sizes, one material, ten pills, plus a load sequence that moves from white editorial layout to a full-bleed dark film with no cut. Every element floats on one surface.
watch_out: Without a truly high-end render the same structure is an empty dark page with a blurry background.

name: Stripe Pricing

type.note: One variable family at custom weights (button text 425). Sizes 13/14/15/16/18/26/38/56.

thesis: A 23,000px rate card made navigable and calm by turning pricing into a well-indexed reference document under one vivid hero moment.
why_made: Everything hangs off visible 270px column guides, tables use a strict navy, grey and purple hierarchy, and navigation stays pinned with progress feedback. The only loud colour is the single gradient ribbon.
watch_out: The diagonal ribbon is cheap without the real shader; a flat CSS rainbow behind cards turns the page into a 2018 template.

name: Otter

type.note: Light 300 for all headings, heavier weights reserved for buttons and labels. Radii scale fluidly (15.6/23.4/31.2).

thesis: A meeting assistant makes a voice product visible through soft grainy gradients and waveform-like shapes on a clean white and cobalt system.
why_made: Light-weight headings against heavy blue buttons give clear hierarchy, and grain stops the pastels banding. Real UI crops and video sit in the same radius family as the gradient tiles.
watch_out: Pastel gradient cards turn to generic AI wallpaper without grain, real product crops and a stronger second colour.

name: Wealthfront

type.note: GT Alpina light italic is the second voice, used for the emotional half of a heading.

thesis: A fintech leads with one huge number, then softens it with a light italic line, on a deep violet field.
why_made: The pairing of heavy Calibre facts and thin GT Alpina italics gives a voice, and warm candid client photography keeps purple fintech from going cold.
watch_out: Sans-plus-italic pairs are now a cliche; here it survives only because the bold half is a real number at extreme scale.

name: Revolut

type.note: Aeonik for headings, plan names and inline bold balance figures; Inter for all reading text. Sizes 12/14/16/18/24/52/88.

thesis: A bank sold as a lifestyle object: full-bleed photography and machined black-and-steel renders with interface floating on top, no chrome around it.
why_made: Imagery is art-directed to one studio standard, and the app UI is laid directly on photos as a thin outline instead of a mockup. One pill shape and a hard white, charcoal and black value ladder do the rest.
watch_out: Overlaying UI on photos only works with a clean subject and calm background; on busy stock it becomes clutter.

name: jemmic

type.note: Geist Pixel Square appears on single emphasised words, Geist Mono uppercase 12px on buttons. Three cuts of one family, so it stays quiet.

thesis: A Swiss bank-software vendor turns data-security cues (halftone, ciphertext, ruled cells) into a precise identity in one saturated blue.
why_made: A visible cell grid runs through light and blue sections alike, and motifs such as pixel type and dot-matrix hands reuse the same square unit. Blue is treated as a full surface with its own keyline tints.
watch_out: Ruled grids everywhere can feel like a Figma frame; they need real content density and exact alignment or they look unfinished.

name: Slack

type.note: Geometric display against a humanist text face; display also used for pills and stat numerals.

thesis: A mature product page where a rebuilt, animated Slack window is the hero and every section is a guided tour of the real interface.
why_made: Product demos are rebuilt to look exactly like the app and are placed on a strict white and aubergine rhythm with a consistent chapter system. Mature but less restrained than top-tier: dense and uppercase-button corporate.
watch_out: Scripted chat demos need real-feeling content; lorem-style messages in a fake window immediately look like a template.

name: Codecademy

type.note: Suisse mono carries section heads and labels with wide tracking; Apercu carries reading text.

thesis: A learn-to-code platform that frames everything as a terminal: mono headings, slash commands and dot fields, warmed by large people photography.
why_made: Terminal cues are confined to headlines, labels and textures while body stays readable, and yellow is reserved for action. Rebuilt IDE tours and hatched cards show real attention to detail.
watch_out: Neon glow, mono type and dot grids together easily collapse into hacker cliche; here warm photography is what prevents that.

name: CockroachDB

type.note: Geist Mono carries buttons, eyebrows, the marquee and dashboards; lime and cyan highlight single phrases in light-weight headings.

thesis: A database company draws its continuum as one interlocking puzzle silhouette that glows violet behind everything.
why_made: The puzzle-edged black mask is a proprietary motif that runs from hero to closing band to faint background outlines. Geist at weight 200 keeps a very loud colour elegant.
watch_out: Violet glow, lime words and cyan stats together become crypto-site noise unless one strict motif holds them.

name: Plausible

type.note: No web font at all, which suits a page arguing for lightness; tight tracking at weight 800 gives the stack its voice.

thesis: A privacy analytics tool sells by showing its actual dashboard, then by writing a long letter from the founders.
why_made: The real product sits in the hero at full legibility, and the pricing slider ties price directly to traffic. Function and candour earn trust rather than visual polish.
watch_out: Stock Tailwind styling, a system font and indigo read as default unless product and copy carry real substance.

name: North Hub Partners

type.note: A newspaper serif for statements, geometric sans for labels and body. Single radius of 8px across the page.

thesis: A Brazilian corporate finance boutique is presented through vast aerial photography and calm scroll pacing on icy blue.
why_made: One inset nav, one photo frame and one pale ground make stock-grade images feel curated. Scroll staging gives it a pace most pages at this level lack.
watch_out: Imagery here is stock or AI-grade, and large serif words over busy photos lose legibility without a scrim.

name: Strapi

type.note: One family; section heads go heavier and tighter than the hero. Dark hero hands over to a white page.

thesis: An open-source CMS organises its hero as a bordered sheet of cells holding pitch, install command, logos and live admin UI in one frame.
why_made: The hairline-cell hero packs four jobs into one structured block, and real admin screens appear in tinted panels on the way down. The command field replaces a button as primary action.
watch_out: Poppins plus a purple sparkle banner pulls it toward template; the cell grid needs thin, low-contrast lines and strict alignment to feel engineered.

name: Apple

type.note: Two optical cuts of one family. 12px for nav, footer and legal; 21-28px subheads; nothing decorative.

thesis: A front page built as a wall of posters: each tile is one product, one line, two buttons and one extraordinary image.
why_made: A single tile template repeats without variation, with one blue and a 12px white seam, so image quality does the remaining work. That discipline lets a lease offer and a flagship laptop share one grid.
watch_out: The formula depends on museum-grade product imagery; with ordinary pictures it becomes a stack of empty banners.

name: Trasti Ubezpieczenia. Simply fair!

type.note: Inter Display for large sizes; red appears only as pen marks, icons and primary actions.

thesis: An insurer made friendly with a red pen: hand-drawn line art, sketched underlines and warm people photography on a strict white grid.
why_made: Custom monoline illustrations give a commodity product its own hand, while navy Inter headlines and uniform hairline cards stay rigorous.
watch_out: Blobs and floating cards go cheap quickly; keep the line art bespoke and the blob tint barely visible.

name: Neon Pricing

type.note: GeistMono uppercase only for data keys. Radius 4 or pill, nothing in between.

thesis: A pricing page built as a technical datasheet: conjoined hairline cells, mono keys and one green signal.
why_made: The tier grid has zero radius and zero gap, so it reads as an engineering spec rather than marketing, and the long comparison table handles sub-labels with real care. Width shifts between grid and table keep it just short of gold.
watch_out: A black page of hairlines looks unfinished without real information density in every cell.

name: Increase

type.note: Input Mono for terminals, dates and attributions. Every heading is a bold sentence running on into a light grey sentence.

thesis: Treats a bank as infrastructure: a drawn page grid, monospaced system artefacts and one huge folded brand mark replace sales theatre.
why_made: Every fake product surface is a fully designed fragment with plausible data, and all of it sits on one visible set of rail lines running through light and dark bands. Two-tone run-on headings carry the narrative with no eyebrows.
watch_out: Without real data density in the fragments, rail lines and mono labels become empty dev-tool costume.

name: Apple Design

type.note: Lighter than apple.com: no display extremes, hierarchy from 40, 24 and 17 only.

thesis: A design-resources hub whose hero makes the interface itself the subject: glass controls rendered as exploded, lens-like objects.
why_made: One render, complete with construction circles and refraction, demonstrates the craft being taught, then the page drops to flat, strict tiles that get out of the way.
watch_out: Below the hero it is a plain card directory; copying the cards without a signature hero reads as a generic docs index.

name: Ramp

type.note: One family at regular weight throughout; hierarchy comes from size and black-to-grey. Mono only inside globe tags.

thesis: A finance platform sold as calm automation: one loud lime on warm off-white, huge amounts of believable product, and a story that turns chaos into a single window.
why_made: A single regular-weight grotesque, a strict warm 12px panel and lime reserved for action create restraint, while every panel holds dense, animated, plausible product. Live counters make the page feel as if it is running.
watch_out: Copying lime and off-white without the dense product work leaves a sparse page with a loud button.

name: Radix UI

type.note: soehneMono for code. A book serif at -5% tracking is the one surprise on a UI page.

thesis: A component library argues by showing: the first screen is its own components, working, stacked beside a one-column pitch.
why_made: The desktop page is a single viewport: a classical serif pitch left, real functional kits right on a faceted pastel ground. Serif against dense interface makes a refined contrast.
watch_out: Serif plus pastel turns twee unless the components are production quality and perfectly aligned.

name: Obsidian

type.note: Inter-style stack with heavy negative tracking at display size; links in lighter ~#a78bfa.

thesis: A knowledge app shows its real interface, in dark, at size, with no gradient or glow beyond one crystal.
why_made: The real app window fills the hero's base with a phone overlapped, and each feature card holds a genuine crop. One violet and short period-ended headlines keep it confident.
watch_out: Flat grey-on-near-black cards turn monotonous without real UI to show in each.

name: Raycast Store

type.note: Positive tracking of ~0.2-0.4px runs through body and UI text, which is unusual and keeps 13-15px grey legible on near-black.

thesis: An extension marketplace that behaves like a native dark app: one blurred brand light at the top, then a calm, dense catalogue of tiles.
why_made: Three near-black steps separate page, card and raised card with no shadows, and every listing repeats one exact metadata rhythm. App-icon tiles dim and blur toward the edges, giving the hero depth without a product shot.
watch_out: Grey on near-black falls below readable fast and the sub copy here is already at the limit, so a loose copy turns to mush.

name: Temporal

type.note: Noto Sans Mono carries every button, eyebrow and diagram label; body copy is lavender rather than grey.

thesis: A durable-execution pitch that proves itself with a runnable failure demo, set in light grotesk over black with square mono controls.
why_made: The contrast of very light 68px type against hard-edged mono buttons gives it a voice, and the live demo shows the product instead of claiming it. Hairline square cards and neon diagrams share one system.
watch_out: Light-weight display type with -2px tracking and 24px lavender body gets tiring over 13000px; the long uniform left-column rhythm drifts into monotony.

name: Function Health

type.note: Fragment Mono appears only at 9-12px for chart labels and motion controls, which keeps the clinical data voice small.

thesis: A consumer health membership made to feel like a calm, premium medical journal: warm paper, serif statements and tiny, exact data graphics.
why_made: One colour, one headline device and one card language run for 12000px without tiring, and each section gets its own structure (ruled table, masonry, gradient column). UI fragments are redrawn for the page at real fidelity rather than pasted as screenshots.
watch_out: The roman-plus-italic accent headline is everywhere now; without a real serif and this much restraint in colour it reads as a wellness template.

name: Sora

type.note: The URL lands on a help-centre article about the product's discontinuation, so this card covers article furniture, not a product page.

thesis: A plain help article held to brand standard with one typeface, a strict column and almost no chrome.
why_made: Black underline search, a bold-on-active contents rail and quiet hairline cards give a support template the same tone as the marketing site. Nothing is decorated.
watch_out: With no imagery the page depends on spacing and a good typeface; set in a default font it is an unstyled help-desk template.

name: Prisma

type.note: Sora stays in headings and the footer wordmark; Inter carries everything else at slightly open tracking.

thesis: A TypeScript platform pitch tied together by one object: the logo's three-colour ribbon, threaded through panels, 3D renders and the footer wordmark.
why_made: The ribbon gives a conventional SaaS page a memorable system, and the marbled paper texture stops the white from feeling default. Mock UI is redrawn with skeleton bars at consistent scale.
watch_out: Spectral glow, sparkly 3D glass and marble texture at once sits close to AI-startup excess; remove the ribbon's discipline and it is just rainbow gradients.

name: Twilio

type.note: Generous 20px body throughout; a pixel-style display face appears only inside result numerals.

thesis: An enterprise communications platform on deep navy, turning each product into one tall tile with a redrawn UI fragment.
why_made: Fragments share a strict recipe of navy fill, 2px white outline and a single red active chip, which keeps a large product line coherent. Blue and red never compete: blue acts, red highlights.
watch_out: The large proactive chat widget covers ~20% of every frame, and many pill CTAs of equal weight flatten the hierarchy.

name: Sam Hoult Beauty

type.note: Tight negative tracking on a high-contrast serif gives it weight at this size; Figtree handles small UI.

thesis: A home nail salon presented with high-street calm: big serif, bronze accents and an honest price list.
why_made: The price panels are the best part, a plain real document laid out well, and the macro nail photo gives the hero a craft signal most local sites lack. A single bronze keeps stock and customer photos together.
watch_out: Template bones show: indented hero copy, a nav link crossing the photo edge, and mixed stock and phone photos that need heavy curation.

name: Energen Digital

type.note: Secondary accent is pink #e9557f; Bricolage's odd shapes do the characterful work while Manrope stays neutral.

thesis: A one-person agency sells rebrands to accountants with loud sticker-like confidence, proving the promise with a live before-and-after hero.
why_made: The hero is the portfolio: a real slider showing a firm's old site turning into a new one, with metrics that change alongside it. Violet, pink and ink are used as whole surfaces rather than as trim.
watch_out: Hard offset shadows, marker highlights and pill badges are the neo-brutal Framer kit; without the demo and sector-specific copy it looks like any template.

name: Decagon

type.note: Measured largest text is the 124px stat at -4.96px; section headings run 40px at normal weight, never bold.

thesis: An enterprise AI agent sold as hospitality: a dreamy periwinkle travel scene up front, then a tightly managed product story on stacked rounded sheets.
why_made: An art-directed scene replaces the usual dashboard hero, and everything after it is calm: one violet, one label device, one sheet radius. Abstract concepts become glass objects that show how the product works.
watch_out: The scene only works with real art direction and a uniform sky; a generic AI image with a gradient button on it looks exactly like what this is avoiding.

name: LaunchDarkly

type.note: A mono face labels dashboard tiles. Hero runs ~84px with very tight leading despite the measured 1.2 line-height elsewhere.

thesis: A feature-flag platform restyled as a punk sticker sheet: acid lime, cut-corner shapes and a grinning mascot layered over real dashboards.
why_made: Everything shares one shape language of notches, mixed radii and hard outlines, so the noise reads as a system. The nav itself is cut into the page, a rare and very specific idea.
watch_out: Sparkles, mascots and neon stacked with a proactive chat bubble tip into chaos, and this kind of shape language is wrong for most enterprise briefs.

name: Attio Pricing

type.note: Weights stay at 500-600 and nothing exceeds 56px; hierarchy is built from size steps and grey values.

thesis: A pricing page treated as a precise reference document: four plain cards, then a huge matrix that stays usable the whole way down.
why_made: Radius, hairline and grey values are exact and repeated, one soft blue is the only colour, and the sticky header solves the real problem of long comparison tables. It feels like the product UI.
watch_out: Copied at lower precision (uneven hairlines, default shadows, loose rows) this is just a generic white pricing table.

name: Remote

type.note: One family at all sizes; heavy, very tight display sizes look nearly italic against the bold round wordmark.

thesis: Payroll software made unmistakable: the wordmark fills the hero and the page colour travels from violet to aqua to lime and back as you scroll.
why_made: A serious B2B product takes one loud, ownable idea, the scrolling hue journey, and keeps the components underneath quite orderly. Ultra-tight bold type gives it a real voice.
watch_out: Saturated full-page gradients hurt legibility and turn neon fast; without the custom wordmark and strict white cards this reads as a Y2K template.

name: GoPro

type.note: Extended heavy caps carry all headlines and buttons; plain Sohne handles specs and prices.

thesis: A retail homepage run like an active-sport magazine: loud wide caps, big action photos and rail after rail of products on cool grey tiles.
why_made: A single display face and consistent grey product tile keep a promo-heavy page in order, and the real user footage does the emotional work.
watch_out: Too many sections and auto-rotating carousels of equal weight; hard promo copy and tile repetition make it feel like a sale flyer rather than a brand page.

name: Expo

type.note: JetBrains Mono appears only in 12px captions and one inline code chip.

thesis: Mobile infrastructure sold on a calm white page where soft squircle cards, app-icon geometry and real product fragments carry the pitch.
why_made: One ink, one pale card tone and one 40px radius repeat everywhere, so variety comes from content. Product fragments dissolve into cards through masks instead of hard crops, and -3px tracking gives Inter a drawn quality.
watch_out: Crushed tracking below display sizes, or 40px radii with added borders and shadows, collapses straight into generic AI-SaaS bento.

name: Cognition

type.note: GeistMono only in the 12px footer. Largest type on the page is 36px.

thesis: A research lab's homepage that reads like a typeset memo: left-rail index, serif prose, ruled columns and almost no marketing devices.
why_made: 36px is the largest type, radii are zero, and visible hairline columns with tick caps make the layout feel drafted. Proof arrives as real data, a benchmark table and named logos, rather than illustration.
watch_out: Without serious prose and real proof, the empty ruled columns and small type read as an unstyled docs page.

name: Browserbase

type.note: gtStandardMono carries labels, inline tags and links; gtPlanar reaches 104px for one stat.

thesis: Browser infrastructure for agents drawn as a blueprint, with the web rendered as dithered pixel terrain.
why_made: Exposed rules, mono labels and schematic UI give engineering rigour, while one bitmap treatment repeats across hero, CRT and steps, so loud colour reads as a system rather than decoration.
watch_out: Acid dithered landscapes plus highlighter headlines become retro gimmick noise unless the grid and mono details are equally disciplined.

name: Talkspace

type.note: Serif headlines in teal rather than black; old-style figures on stats.

thesis: Online therapy warmed up with pastel colour fields, a soft serif and real member portraits, with insurance coverage as the repeated promise.
why_made: Notched colour cards and named member photography give the page a recognisable shape, and a strict two-font system holds the many pastels together.
watch_out: Pastel fills on every section become a children's-app patchwork if the deep teal anchor and real photography are removed.

name: Lemon Squeezy

type.note: Display never goes bolder than Book; Inter carries all body copy.

thesis: A payments platform in Stripe-era colour blocking: saturated violet hero, then white pages broken by two-tone stages holding product fragments.
why_made: Coded section numbering such as E/1 and M/2, sharp UI fragments on flat colour and strict module reuse give a 19,000px page clear structure.
watch_out: The tilted device hero and flat saturated blocks date quickly if the UI inside is not sharp and real.

name: Teenage Engineering

type.note: Proprietary faces. Caps TechnoType for the monologue, thin lowercase te-20 for navigation.

thesis: A product launch staged as a darkroom joke, where a spotlit device casts an absurdly long shadow that becomes the page.
why_made: One render, one light and deadpan copy carry everything. The line-glyph header feels drawn by industrial designers and owes nothing to a UI kit.
watch_out: A one-idea page fails outright if the render is not flawless or the joke is flat, and it conveys almost no product information.

name: Headspace

type.note: Single family at every level; hero H1 renders ~52/60, with 72px reserved for the closing CTA.

thesis: Mental health made friendly through a round orange character world, sunshine yellow and soft pill shapes that make signing up feel low-stakes.
why_made: A proprietary rounded face runs through logo, illustration and even the ticker, so brand stays consistent, and the two-path hero routes users quickly.
watch_out: Smiley shapes and bubbly radii turn childish for any brand without Headspace's owned character system.

name: Scale AI

type.note: Weight 400 only; section headings run 64/67.2 -0.64px. A mono face handles labels at 11-13px.

thesis: Reliable AI positioned as serious infrastructure, moving from annotated real-world video to a black stage, then sheets of forest green, grey and tan.
why_made: Regular-weight Aeonik at large sizes with tight 8-16px radii keeps it sober, while computer-vision annotations make visuals evidence of the product. Sections stack as physical sheets, the previous one dimming behind.
watch_out: Long black stretches and scroll-locked panes feel empty and slow unless pane art and copy reveals are precise.

name: Medusa622: Luxury Skin & Nails in Knightsbridge

type.note: Romie italic is used only for connector words. The footer wordmark reaches 426px.

thesis: A Knightsbridge salon dressed as a quiet luxury brand: high-contrast serif, plum text links and warm macro photography on near-white.
why_made: One serif, one sans, no buttons and no radii give it confidence, while small italic connectors and full-bleed staggered photos add refinement over a short 6,000px page.
watch_out: High-contrast serifs over saturated, uneven imagery slide into a beauty template the moment the photography loses consistency.

name: OpenRouter

type.note: Gordita only on the H1; Plus Jakarta Sans carries everything else including 36px stats.

thesis: A developer marketplace homepage that behaves like product UI: compact nav, plain stats and live model data cards on near-white.
why_made: Consistent 8px hairline cards, real numbers and one violet accent keep it tidy, and live data lifts it above the template skeleton.
watch_out: This skeleton of centred headline, four stats and four cards turns generic instantly without real live numbers.

name: Calvyn

type.note: Serif for headings, Inter for all UI. Geist appears in small interface text; neutrals are Apple-like.

thesis: An AI research firm that borrows Apple-style neutrals and a bookish serif to feel like a trusted consultancy rather than a chatbot vendor.
why_made: Two-tone serif headlines, dash eyebrows and real interview UI repeat with discipline, and blue grain stages give every product shot the same lit setting.
watch_out: Tightly tracked Merriweather over 20,000px of repeated modules drifts toward long-form template if the demos stop being real.

name: Hotjar

type.note: Captured URL redirects to contentsquare.com/hotjar; the page is the post-merger migration landing.

thesis: A migration page that explains Hotjar becoming Contentsquare through direct comparison, with plum and coral product fragments.
why_made: The direct feature comparison and notched product cards are specific to the product, and a disciplined plum-to-pink palette holds the page together.
watch_out: Redirect-page devices such as the sticky bottom bar and stacked CTAs feel pushy if carried into a normal homepage.

name: Attio

type.note: Section heads ~40px weight 500 in two inks. Tiempos Text 48px/52px appears once, for the pull quote. JetBrains Mono only inside terminal and SQL fragments.

thesis: A CRM sold by running the real product on a single ruled page, with a two-tone headline voice and one dark chapter for the platform story.
why_made: Two page rails and shared hairlines hold every section to one grid, and the demos are live HTML UI with believable data. Blue is rationed to active states, so the near-monochrome page feels instrumented.
watch_out: Rails and cells feel like empty scaffolding if the demos inside them are static or the data looks fake.

name: Visora

type.note: Section heads step 58px/61.5px and 50px/54px with proportional negative tracking. All Inter, so the renders carry the identity.

thesis: A concept AI vision product that swaps product UI for an isometric factory render and scrambled-text motion.
why_made: A disciplined one-accent dark system with consistent card recipes, and motion that shows care in load and type. It is a template-grade structure well executed.
watch_out: AI-looking renders and glass cards over busy footage read as generic concept work if there is no real product behind them.

name: Oxygen Pictures

type.display: Bebas Neue Pro Expanded Bold, 100px/96px, -3px, uppercase
type.note: Geist SemiBold jumps to 248px/210.8px at -12.4px for one marquee. The display jump from 18px to 100px and 248px does most of the design work.

thesis: A German video studio that frames its reel with hard white gutters, square black buttons and one enormous line of type.
why_made: Radius zero, one ink and footage as the only colour give it conviction, and the logo's stepped pixel shape returns as the outline pattern behind the CTA.
watch_out: Large empty cells and square blocks turn into a bare wireframe if the footage is not excellent.

name: LiveKit

type.text: Public Sans, 16px with 18-20px leads, wide-ish letterfit
type.note: Mono carries eyebrows, code, stats and diagram labels. Section heads 36px weight 300. Low weight on black is the signature.

thesis: Realtime voice infrastructure drawn as a technical blueprint: thin type, wire diagrams and one electric cyan on near-black.
why_made: Radii stop at 8px, depth comes from two blacks and 1px hairlines, and the diagrams explain the product through scroll. Cyan is confined to one flat button and glowing keywords.
watch_out: Glowing words become cheap neon if the weight rises or they appear in more than a few places per heading.

name: Boom

type.note: Simplon BP Mono 16px uppercase in pale yellow is the only second voice. H2s drop to 48px/51.8px weight 400.

thesis: An aerospace manufacturer told as a cinematic reel of machining, turbines and aircraft under one wide-caps line.
why_made: The wide-caps and yellow-mono lockup never moves while footage changes underneath, which gives heavy industry a calm authority. Most stops show the same lockup, so only part of the long page could be judged.
watch_out: A single lockup over a video reel has no substance unless the footage is genuinely owned and shot well.

name: Sentry

type.note: Monaco for code and fragments. H2s 60px/66px. Copy runs weight 600+ at 24-27px, which is loud by design.

thesis: An error-monitoring platform with a comic-book voice, inky mascots and a purple nebula, which treats its developers as an in-group.
why_made: The illustration system, jokes and gradient borders are consistent and clearly drawn in-house. Pink, lime and violet are used with rules, even at this volume.
watch_out: Without commissioned illustration and a real voice, this palette and tilted type collapse into a noisy purple template.

name: Comet

type.display: GT Canon VF, 90px/90px, 900 axis name (renders light), -2.5px
type.note: Section heads 64px/76.8px at -0.7px, closer 80px at -1.6px. GT Standard Mono only in the footer.

thesis: An AI browser presented as a calm paper page in orbit, with grainy planets and hairline trajectories around a condensed editorial serif.
why_made: One invented object, the grain planet, carries from hero to footer, and soft paper surfaces use shadow and noise instead of borders. Teal stays reserved for the product itself.
watch_out: Space imagery and textured spheres turn into stock sci-fi if the planets lose their grain or crowd the copy.

name: Apptronik

type.note: Section heads 32px/39px weight 400. Nav and labels 13px uppercase with ~0.2em tracking. Weight 300 keeps the robot brand from sounding industrial.

thesis: A humanoid robot maker that presents hardware as calm consumer product, with rounded tiles of studio and warehouse photography.
why_made: One tile recipe of radius 15px and #eee or photo runs the whole page, and the studio-grey robot shots do real work. Orange is held back to the single nav action and small press labels.
watch_out: Text-heavy grey tiles look like a default bento if the photography is ordinary.

name: Kata.ai

type.note: H2 40px/44px at -2px. In the capture the manifesto and stat numerals fall back to Arial, a visible flaw.

thesis: Enterprise AI presented with graded photography, sky-blue gradients and calm cards, for a regional corporate buyer.
why_made: The light DM Sans, tight tracking and a tidy tab frame feel current, and the stacked image deck is a real idea. Font fallbacks and many generic AI-looking photos keep it below top tier.
watch_out: AI-generated stock portraits and full-colour logos in grey boxes quickly read as an enterprise template.

name: React

type.note: Source Code Pro for code at ~14px. Rendered heading leading looks ~60px at section level.

thesis: A documentation home that teaches the concept while it sells it, pairing real code with its rendered result.
why_made: The code-and-output pairs are the argument, and the plain type and teal ink stay out of the way. It is clear and generous, though not distinctive enough for top tier.
watch_out: Long centred paragraphs and pale bands become flat if there is no real example in each section.

name: Ritual

type.note: Dutch801 Roman italic swaps in for key phrases and role titles. Metropolis appears for tracked caps.

thesis: A vitamin brand that makes supply-chain evidence feel joyful through one navy ink, one yellow and very close human photography.
why_made: Navy replaces black everywhere and the capsule-on-yellow product tile is instantly ownable. The serif italic insert gives warmth, though sale banners and busy strips keep it from gold.
watch_out: Saturated yellow beside skin tones goes loud fast, so it needs white space and art direction to hold.

name: i-D and Ray-Ban present RED

type.display: Arial Narrow Bold, 230/184, weight 400 (bold cut), -6.9px, uppercase
type.text: A-OTF Midashi Min, 40/~44 for manifesto and 55px for questions, 20px small text
type.note: A hard pairing of condensed grotesque caps with a high-contrast serif, both in one red. Telidon pixel face only for a tiny credit.

thesis: A one-colour competition microsite that treats the winning artworks as raw material, building the headline, the layout and the exit out of red.
why_made: The whole system is one red, one mint logo clash and two typefaces, while fixed corner elements hold the page together as wildly different images pass beneath.
watch_out: Without real art to fill the tiles, and without a colour as committed as this red, image-mosaic letters and fixed corner boxes turn into a gimmick that hides content.

name: Inngest

type.note: Four families used by role: Whyte for display, Circular for reading, WhyteMono for nav and buttons in uppercase, CircularXXMono for code. Electric blue #013cf6 is the second accent.

thesis: A durable-execution product page that feels like a printed technical poster: grainy black, mono labels, real run state and one shock of electric blue.
why_made: Every piece of decoration explains the product, from run-state chips on the hero code to a timeline rail, and the grain gives flat dark panels something to be cut out of.
watch_out: Grain, outlined type and pixel dissolves become dark-mode cliches if used without real product content and a strict role for each typeface.

name: motusmade studio

type.note: One family with very tight display tracking; greys and a single green availability dot do all the colour work.

thesis: A one-person studio page for movement educators, where a cutout moving figure carries a clean white template into its niche.
why_made: The recurring cutout dancer and tilted process cards add a specific idea to otherwise disciplined white-and-grey layout.
watch_out: Remove the cutout figure and tilted cards and this is a standard Framer template with tight Inter.

name: UNITO

type.text: Roobert Medium, 16/~20; Azeret Mono for labels at ~14px
type.note: Friendly wide sans paired with mono uppercase tags that read like product part labels. Olive #393c23 is the brand ink, used for wordmark and arrow discs.

thesis: A modular shelf brand whose page borrows the logic of its product: a pegboard grid, swappable shapes and one lime surprise at the end.
why_made: The rail pattern, mixed image masks and nested radius system all come from the object being sold, and the quiet near-white lets product renders carry the colour.
watch_out: Very large radii plus pastel tags go twee fast without strong product renders, and the always-on toast shows how a persistent overlay eats the layout.

name: Material 3

type.note: Section headings 57px; a soft variable weight of 475 keeps large type round rather than heavy. Tracking stays normal.

thesis: A design-system home that dogfoods its own tokens: tonal surfaces, a navigation rail and live components at oversized scale.
why_made: Everything comes from one tonal palette and a named radius scale, so a page full of different cards still reads as one system.
watch_out: Outside Google's system this look reads as default Android: lilac everywhere, big radii, no point of view.

name: Rabbit

type.text: Power Grotesk ~22/33 for lead copy; Archivo 17/~28 for small body
type.note: Everything lowercase, even after full stops. Ultralight wide display at huge size, with the same face used for buttons so a CTA reads like a headline.

thesis: A product launch built from two colours and one very thin wide typeface, with photography graded to match the grey page.
why_made: Grey and orange are held with real discipline, and the type scale is pushed far enough that the button, the FAQ and the headline all share one voice.
watch_out: Thin orange type on mid grey is low contrast, and the near-empty one-line screens look unfinished without this level of photography.

name: Make

type.note: One family throughout. Text is tinted aubergine #342237 rather than black, which ties type to the purple surfaces.

thesis: A polished automation SaaS page that moves from airy white lilac into a dark aubergine finish, using persona cards and glass UI chips.
why_made: Consistent 1200px container, tinted text colour and careful card build-ups make a large enterprise page feel controlled.
watch_out: Lilac gradients, glass chips and stock-style people photos are close to generic AI-SaaS, so the craft is in the spacing and not the idea.

name: ConceptCore

type.note: Ultra-condensed poster caps with 403 Degrad Mono labels and neutral Golos body. Leading on body text is unusually tight.

thesis: A concept-art course catalogue dressed as a game interface, with clipped polygons, acid lime and an ultra-condensed poster face.
why_made: One angled cut is applied consistently to buttons, tags, section seams and socials, so a loud look still feels engineered.
watch_out: Clipped corners and acid lime on black are the default gamer look; without consistent geometry and real art this turns into a cheap esports template.

name: Strava

type.note: A proprietary sans used at modest sizes; the logged-out home is a sign-up screen, so type stays functional.

thesis: A logged-out home reduced to one job, sign up, framed by outdoor photography on both sides.
why_made: The three-panel composition gives a plain form real presence, and orange is rationed to the one action and the route line.
watch_out: A form between two photos only works with strong documentary images; stock photos would make it feel like a generic gate page.

name: Accel

type.text: Poppins, 16/~24 weight 300; IBM Plex Mono-style caps for one button
type.note: A serif logo sits against light geometric sans. Sage button colour is the only tint on the page.

thesis: A venture firm's home cut down to one sentence, one news card and a search button.
why_made: Hairline rules under each headline line and the removal of almost everything make a light geometric typeface feel considered.
watch_out: Poppins Light is common, and with so little on screen any spacing error shows immediately.

name: Render

type.text: PP Neue Montreal, 18/~29; PP Neue Montreal Mono for code and tags
type.note: Tracking stays about -3% on all headings down to 32px. Weight 500 for everything; hierarchy comes from size and #0d0d0d to #4d4d4d to #6b6b6b.

thesis: A cloud platform page on crisp white with near-square controls, where real UI fragments and one grainy violet landscape carry all the atmosphere.
why_made: A 2px radius, 1px hairlines and strict type colour steps give engineering sharpness, while grain and gradient-wipe headings stop it feeling cold.
watch_out: The gradient text works only as a transient reveal; left on permanently, or with soft 12px cards, this becomes every purple AI landing page.

name: Continue

type.note: Plex Mono only for spaced uppercase labels. Page is a farewell notice after acquisition, so type stays at letter scale.

thesis: A company farewell page set like a short letter next to a large ink-and-watercolour drawing.
why_made: Modest type at a strict measure lets one remarkable illustration provide all the emotion and quality.
watch_out: Take away the commissioned-quality artwork and this is a plain text page.

name: GitHub Docs

type.note: Mona Sans only on H1, H2 (28px/480) and small heads; system stack for links and body; Mona Sans Mono for tiny caps footer labels.

thesis: A documentation home reduced to one search band and a ruled index of links, with a single pixel-block illustration as its only flourish.
why_made: Every block sits inside a continuous hairline frame, so a plain list of blue links reads as an instrument panel. A tight, light 64px H1 carries the whole brand.
watch_out: Without the ruled frame and the tight display weight this is a default link dump.

name: Bear

type.note: Custom rounded humanist sans whose regular weight reads bold; dark grey rather than black; subheads 22px grey; section titles recoloured per feature.

thesis: A notes app sold through warmth: a soft custom sans, a hand-drawn bear and large organic colour fields carrying tilted fragments of the real app.
why_made: The illustration system holds together from grey line drawings to the mascot, and the blob hues echo the app's own themes. Every fragment shows real note content rather than placeholder bars.
watch_out: Blobs and mascots drift into 2018 template art unless the line work is bespoke and the UI inside is real.

name: Isolabella della Croce

type.note: Switzer at 12px for labels and buttons, 16px for one quote and hours; italic serif in red for the wordmark; no third family.

thesis: A Piedmont wine estate told in Italian through saturated close-up photography and one quiet book serif on warm paper white.
why_made: One serif at one weight, sharp rectangular buttons, nothing else: photography holds all the colour. Large crops alternate with deliberately empty paper.
watch_out: With stock photos or rounded buttons the restraint becomes an empty template.

name: Primer

type.note: H2 34/44.2 weight 500, section heads 28px, card titles 22px; two-tone emphasis via em without italics.

thesis: A design-system home that proves the system by composing its own parts: real components and mascots inside quiet white cards.
why_made: H2s set a grey lead against a black product name, and the art is actual Primer pieces shown as a spec sheet. One corner gradient supplies all the brand colour.
watch_out: Without real component artwork, white cards on grey is a default docs landing.

name: Noxus

type.note: Ginka Light for larger numerals; mono uppercase for eyebrows and metric labels; H2 42px, panel titles 36px.

thesis: Enterprise agents made approachable with one dusty blue, warm workplace portraits and actual workflow screens.
why_made: A single blue runs from the cycling headline word to tile pattern to panels, and mono eyebrows add a technical register beside a humanist display face.
watch_out: A form modal covered the right third of every desktop frame in this capture; a persistent popup like it hides the page and cheapens it.

name: PostHog

type.note: ui-monospace at 11-13px for event data; Source Code Pro for code; pixel-LCD numerals as a detail; 72px only on the logo lockup.

thesis: The marketing site is a full desktop operating system with windows, icons and a hedgehog world, so the personality is the page.
why_made: The OS metaphor is followed through: window chrome, scrollbar, desktop icons and tabs, with deep real product UI inside. The jokes are written as carefully as the layouts are built.
watch_out: The desktop shell without this volume of real UI and writing is a gimmick that hides the product.

name: Lithic

type.note: One family. H2 32/38.4 -0.64px; 24px and 20px for cards and quotes; weight 500 on all headings, 400 for reading text.

thesis: Card infrastructure made tangible: one contour-line motif, taken from the card's own pattern, runs through black, warm, lilac, mint and peach panels.
why_made: Every chapter is a rounded panel in its own low-chroma tint carrying the same hairline drawing, so a pastel system feels owned. A single grotesk at weight 500 keeps the voice terse.
watch_out: Without one owned motif, tinted rounded panels collapse into a pastel bento template.

name: Buildkite

type.note: H2 36/40 -0.9px; hero H1 weight 400 tracking normal; Input Mono for violet eyebrows and footer heads; body and UI fragments on the system stack.

thesis: CI presented as an engineering document: a ruled matrix of small live diagrams beneath a purple-night customer-proof hero.
why_made: Each grid cell holds a bespoke miniature UI built for that one claim rather than a screenshot. Violet, kite green and the mono eyebrow come straight from the product.
watch_out: The hero's logos, phone and glass panels turn to noise without strict z-order and one customer story at a time.

name: Stripe Payments

type.note: H2 38/48 -0.2px; card titles 26px; 15px for buttons at weight 425; body 15/24 inside cards; Source Code Pro only in code.

thesis: A product page built like documentation: every claim gets a real working product fragment, framed by a single slanted gradient and a visible column grid.
why_made: A dashed four-column grid is literally drawn under the page and everything aligns to it. Shadows are long, low and blue-tinted, and the fragments are functional UI rather than pictures of UI.
watch_out: The diagonal gradient without real UI and the alignment grid is a 2018 Stripe pastiche.

name: Cloudinary

type.note: Two voices: light Inter for headings, 14px/700 uppercase for nav and buttons; sofia-pro only in the logo.

thesis: An enterprise media platform on navy with lime and cyan, explaining itself through transformation demos and analyst credentials.
why_made: The demos use Cloudinary's actual URL parameters, so they feel engineered. Light display type against bold uppercase controls gives a consistent two-voice system.
watch_out: Mint persona cards with stock headshots and a corner ribbon are template-grade; keep the demos and drop the portraits.

name: Weekstack

type.note: H2 60/61; ghost footer wordmark 198/178; Barlow caps on every heading, Inter with slightly open tracking below.

thesis: An iPhone planner whose page copies its own app: stone and charcoal with a single orange, heavy condensed caps and stacked days.
why_made: Every visual is the real app, restyled into device frames and notification chips. Orange appears only on one heading word, one tile or one glow, so the palette is as restrained as the product.
watch_out: All-caps condensed headlines with one accent word become poster shouting if every section lacks quiet copy beneath.

name: Hawl Design

type.note: All copy lowercased via text-transform; H2 40/44; HawlServices is a custom display face used inside artwork; mono for tiny tags.

thesis: A solo design-engineering subscription sold with quiet dark UI, a lowercase voice and a handful of glossy 3D mascots.
why_made: Two-tone headings and a strict 240-to-1200 column keep it calm, and each section uses its own small mechanic: progress list, gradient timeline, comparison bars. Green is kept for signal.
watch_out: Lowercase two-tone Inter on near-black is a well-worn look; without real case work it is another dark template.

name: Supabase

type.note: Source Code Pro in code cards and mock UI values.

thesis: A quiet developer landing page that explains each product with wire diagrams inside a tight bento, in a 1088px column of white and hairlines.
why_made: Line art, borders and type all share one weight, so a dense product list stays calm. Green only marks actions and live points.
watch_out: Grey wire diagrams go lifeless without motion or real product meaning, and the hot gradient case-study card breaks the calm if used twice.

name: DJI

type.display: Open Sans, 40/44, weight 500; product names are logotype images
type.note: Single family; hierarchy is size only, with bespoke logotypes carrying brand character.

thesis: A hardware catalogue where studio renders and aerial footage do all the work inside a plain centred tile system.
why_made: Every tile shares one image tone and one centred text stack, so a huge range reads as a set. Product imagery is exceptionally controlled.
watch_out: Without photography at this level the same tiles are a dated corporate grid, and three floating widgets at bottom-right clutter the page.

name: Claude Pricing

type.note: Measured scale 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 25, 32, 64. Serif sets names, headings and FAQ questions; sans sets everything operational.

thesis: A pricing page treated as a calm printed document, where warm paper, a serif and ink drawings make a dense comparison feel unhurried.
why_made: One hand-inked drawing system replaces every usual pricing device such as badges, gradients and highlighted columns. The radius, hairline and type scales stay strict through 7,000px of table and FAQ.
watch_out: Without real hand-drawn illustration and a good text serif this collapses into generic beige, and four equal cards need clear naming to steer choice.

name: Paddle

type.note: Condensed serif for all headings and numerals, Inter for body, 12-14px monospace for captions. Capture has a consent panel fixed at lower right.

thesis: Billing software dressed as a confident financial publication, with condensed serif headlines on warm sand and one hit of pure yellow.
why_made: The sand palette holds for most of the page, so the yellow panel lands hard. Stacked sheets, notched cards and ruled footer give ordinary sections distinct construction.
watch_out: The heavy sheet shadows look muddy on lighter stock, and yellow loses its effect if it spreads beyond a few small tiles and one panel.

name: Casper

type.note: Swash alternates of New Kansas appear for campaign lines only.

thesis: A mattress store in full seasonal campaign mode, keeping its soft serif and navy system while a film tie-in takes over the page.
why_made: The storybook cards and lime badge give a sales page real art direction, and soft serif plus pills keep tone friendly across dense merchandising.
watch_out: Stacked promo bands, a fixed offer tab and a chat bubble crowd the first screen, so the campaign reads as busy if copied wholesale.

name: Speakeasy

type.note: Three voices with fixed jobs: hairline serif states, grey sans explains, ABCDiatypeMono uppercase ~14px labels and acts.

thesis: An enterprise AI security page that borrows the ruled sheet of an engineering drawing, setting hairline serif statements against ASCII figures and real product diagrams.
why_made: Every section sits on the same 1px crosshair grid, and each type voice has one job, so the page feels specified rather than decorated. Colour is confined to a thin spectrum rail, one quote mark and small status marks.
watch_out: Weight 100 serif turns frail below ~48px, and the ASCII art reads as a gimmick if it is low density or tinted with brand colour.

name: Sourcegraph

type.note: Poly Sans Mono 14px for eyebrows, tags, footer heads and the hero button.

thesis: A near-black engineering page that alternates dark and light chapters, joined by pixel-tile dissolves and held together by two full-height rails.
why_made: A single frame of hairlines runs through every section, and transitions are pixel events rather than colour changes. Coral is rationed to the nav button, logo and a few product details.
watch_out: The pixel noise and perspective grid become cyberpunk wallpaper if brightened, tinted or placed behind body text.

name: Nurx

type.display: PP Pangram Sans, 88/99.4, weight 600, normal tracking
type.note: Apercu Mono Pro 14px uppercase with wide tracking for labels and lists.

thesis: A women's health service made warm with close-up portraits and peach surfaces, then steadied with black rules and tracked mono labels.
why_made: Black rules and mono labels add clinical order to a soft palette, and photo-to-colour fades let copy sit on imagery without visible boxes.
watch_out: White text on an unscrimmed photo depends on image choice, and long legal copy needs its own contained treatment.

name: lorisbukvic.graphics

type.display: intranet (pixel-cut caps), ~36/37 in hero, 28/36 elsewhere, weight 400
type.note: Pixel face sets all headings; semibold grotesque sets all details at reduced white.

thesis: A Y2K chrome-and-lightning portfolio that treats the site as a desktop, with a dangling metal doll, folder icons and a dock.
why_made: Everything sits on pure black with one electric blue, and 3D, type and icons overlap in depth. Small touches such as bracket button and live status give it a coherent fiction.
watch_out: Chrome and pixel type become a dated cliché without original 3D work, and dim grey text fails on legibility if taken further.

name: IRONHILL

type.note: Expanded GT America ~12px caps for sublabels; PP Woodland digits with dotted zero for the counter.

thesis: A storybook expedition into a mythical place, told as one long scroll along a hand-drawn trail through engravings, slides and field notes.
why_made: One moss ink on one cream paper unites engravings, photos and type, and every motion ties to the trail metaphor. The found objects feel archival rather than decorative.
watch_out: Scroll-locked storytelling is slow for anyone who wants a product, and vintage engraving turns to pastiche without a consistent ink, grain and palette.

name: Key

type.note: Caslon for names and headings; proxima-nova with light tracking for body and caps labels. Capture ends at 2550px where a signup modal stops scrolling.

thesis: A vacation rental brand that sells hosted moments through lifestyle video and Caslon, and keeps its booking form always in reach.
why_made: The search form travels from hero to sticky bar without changing, and the gold rule and Caslon hold a consistent brochure rhythm.
watch_out: Magenta on square boxes feels dated beside the Caslon and gold, and the interrupting modal undoes the calm.

name: Awwwards SOTD

type.note: Nothing on the page exceeds 15px; submitted thumbnails supply all the scale.

thesis: A neutral directory shell that keeps its own chrome at 15px and grey so that loud thumbnails can do all the shouting.
why_made: A two-step grey ladder and two radii hold a dense filter bar together, and small outlined badges carry the only colour the shell owns.
watch_out: Copy the 15px ceiling onto a page without strong imagery and it reads as an unfinished admin screen.

name: Magram

type.note: Uppercase 15px buttons and 13px tracked eyebrows; cream #fcf1e3 replaces white on navy.

thesis: A custom-software studio sold like a law firm: navy ink, square buttons, numbers and blunt French copy instead of decoration.
why_made: A strict 1104px column, one navy, one cream and 1px rules everywhere make long sales content feel orderly. Square CTAs give a plain Albert Sans page some backbone.
watch_out: Bordered boxes in every section drift towards a template, and the form's r10 inputs already disagree with the square buttons.

name: Fenriz Gym

type.note: Roboto 14/700 uppercase on all buttons; measured text styles were unavailable, sizes estimated from frames.

thesis: A Kreuzberg fight gym built from grainy black-and-white photography, a poster condensed face and one gradient used like a logo.
why_made: Colour is rationed to a single brand gradient against strict monochrome photos, so each appearance reads as identity. The hero's photographic slab gives the page its one memorable image.
watch_out: Centred Roboto copy under loud headings is the weak layer; add more gradients or tints and it collapses into a generic gym template.

name: Prototype

type.note: Three voices: ultra-wide black wordmark, tall condensed gothic for all facts, high-contrast italic serif for all asides.

thesis: A creative production house run as a white, ruled index where tall condensed type and full-colour film stills do everything.
why_made: A six-column grid with hairline rules places every word exactly, and scale jumps from 20px to 180px with nothing between. Colour comes only from the film, so the white feels expensive.
watch_out: The empty white only works because the type is exact and footage is real; with stock images or a regular-width sans it becomes an unfinished page.

name: p5.js

type.note: Intro 30px/36px; 14px only for credits. Pink #f1678e fills controls, blue #1e32aa is reserved for one banner.

thesis: An open-source creative-coding home that behaves like a friendly poster: black 1px rules, pink fills and community artwork.
why_made: Everything hangs off one fixed left rail and 1px black rules, so the loud pink feels structured. The friendly National Park face and asterisk give it a personality that templates lack.
watch_out: Three stacked banners and pink controls crowd the first screen; imitated without the rule system it looks like a school portal.

name: Special Production Agency

type.note: One ultra-black condensed cut at every size, including 16px nav.

thesis: A fashion production house showing campaign photography on a white wall, governed by a single ultra-black typeface.
why_made: Images are never cropped into cards or decorated; a fixed band and white margins let world-class stills sit like a gallery hang. The load sequence turns the name into the event.
watch_out: Ghost-grey subtitles overlapping busy images lose legibility, and with lesser photography the white band has nothing to carry it.

name: Block

type.note: Exactly two text styles on the whole page; both regular weight, pure black.

thesis: A holding company's front door reduced to one mark, one sentence and two rows of links on a single centred axis.
why_made: Two type sizes, one colour and one axis, placed so exactly that the emptiness reads as confidence. A proprietary face and a mark that is literally blocks carry all the brand.
watch_out: Without a custom typeface and a strong mark this is just a blank coming-soon page.

name: Beckmans Examensutstallning 2024

type.note: One size only; italic and link blue #1400ff are the whole hierarchy.

thesis: A design college degree show built as a literal spreadsheet, where student work hides in cells until a row is opened.
why_made: The metaphor is held with no exceptions: cell grid, row numbers, frozen header and system-blue links. Commitment and exact grey grid lines keep the joke from becoming a gimmick.
watch_out: It only works as one committed idea for a design audience; any rounded corner or brand colour breaks it, and it is wrong for commercial pages.

name: Pomegranate Health

type.note: Pills use TTCPro bold uppercase with tracking; wordmark is outlined Gliker with a hard extruded shadow.

thesis: Health-AI waitlist page drawn as a warm cartoon system, turning the fruit's rind into layered sheets, pills and outlined widgets.
why_made: Every surface obeys the same plum 1.5px outline, hard shelf shadow and pastel fills, down to phone UI and illustrations. That system consistency separates it from ordinary playful startup pages.
watch_out: Outline-and-shelf styling is charming only across a fully drawn system; applied to a few cards it reads as neo-brutalist template.

name: Deebak Tamilmani Portfolio

type.note: Geist Pixel at 10px for canvas labels; measured sizes run 10-32px, the title size is estimated from frames.

thesis: An architect's portfolio where a scroll-flown point-cloud city is the index and Swiss cream chrome supplies the facts.
why_made: A disciplined cream frame, hard rule and over-tight grotesque contain a very loud WebGL scene. Amber on warm black, with few cyan accents, keeps it restrained and expensive.
watch_out: Without real geometry and fine point density the scene is generic particle noise, and 10px captions are already at the legibility limit.

name: Red Blob Games

type.note: Avenir Next 700 for card titles and heads; system fonts, hyphenated body text.

thesis: A decades-old explainer index where hand-built diagrams are the design and the reading column does the rest.
why_made: Every thumbnail is a real custom diagram, and body type is set with book-grade measure, leading and hyphenation. The craft is in the content; the chrome is older than it should be.
watch_out: The glossy red header bars with text shadows are dated; take the card grid and reading column and leave those behind.

name: White Label IQ

type.note: Scale 14/16/18/24/30/55/65. Sentence-case Avenir Heavy kicker sits over every caps headline.

thesis: A B2B agency-services page that replaces stock visuals with one continuous hand-drawn line threading through every section.
why_made: One black monoline, one orange and one type family keep a 12,500px sales page coherent, and the line physically connects sections. The kicker-over-caps pattern repeats without exception.
watch_out: Monoline doodles become clip art if stroke weight varies or the line simply stops at section borders.

name: Muda 26

type.display: Pixel wordmark drawn on a square grid, ~376×75px
type.note: Sizes 15/16/20/25/32 with weight 400 throughout. Captions run at a size most sites reserve for subheads.

thesis: A digital-art museum's site reduced to a chronological column of works, with a bitmap wordmark and one physical blue ball that reacts to scroll.
why_made: Large captions in one left-offset column keep a 20,000px feed calm, and a single saturated #2b04d1 circle is the only interface colour.
watch_out: An off-axis column on an empty page looks like a broken layout unless the offset is exact and the imagery strong.

name: Three Zero Five Studio

type.note: Only two sizes, 75 and 14. Display letters are bundles of fine hair strokes that shear with wind.

thesis: A London studio whose page is a live instrument: wind data from outside bends the typography itself.
why_made: A custom variable font turns a plain list of names into the identity, and the small mono sidebar and dial explain it with real data.
watch_out: Legibility is deliberately at risk; hair type on anything that must be read quickly is a mistake.

name: Universally Speaking

type.note: A 300-weight caps headline in gradient fill alternates with 800 white caps, so one family covers both loud and quiet.

thesis: A games-QA vendor that borrows the energy of game key art, with gradient fields, gold diagonals and chamfered panels instead of corporate service blocks.
why_made: One ~30 degree angle repeats through the hero band, hairlines and every chamfered card, so a loud palette still reads as a system.
watch_out: Montserrat 800 with a blue-violet gradient and dot grids dates fast; without real game art it is a 2018 template.

name: CITADEL Construction Group

type.display: Bebas Neue, 80px/72px, 200, 1.6px for numerals; Montserrat 800 ~48px +2px caps for heads
type.note: Sizes 11/12/13/16/18/24/36. Condensed logotype supplies the attitude; Montserrat with wide tracking handles everything else.

thesis: A construction holding group pitched in heavy contrast: black, safety orange and a condensed logotype blown up to full screen.
why_made: The scrollspy pill, dot-matrix map and gradient wordmark outro all come from the brand's own parts, and the footer turns partners into a usable directory.
watch_out: White centred paragraph over busy jobsite video has no scrim and loses legibility; copy this only with a real overlay.

name: CSDG Development Group

type.note: Sizes 12/15/16/27/28/48/88/149. The jump from 27px light to 149px bold does all the hierarchy.

thesis: A property developer page built as a ruled ledger of ~360px cells where numbers, claims and images each take a box.
why_made: One black hairline grid does all the organising, and huge Space Grotesk numerals against 12px tracked links give print-like contrast across a short 3,000px page.
watch_out: Hairline cells collapse into a spreadsheet if the type sizes are not this far apart or images lose their inner padding.

name: Acne Studios

type.display: Acne Studios custom geometric wordmark, ~1080px wide on hero and ~215px docked, ~500, tight
type.note: Only two sizes exist on the page, 12 and 18. Uppercase 12px does nav and labels, sentence-case 12px does captions and links. No heading style at all.

thesis: A fashion homepage that removes web convention (headlines, buttons, product metadata) and lets campaign images, two type sizes and a hard 50/50 split carry the store.
why_made: One split line at 720px and a two-size type system govern everything from hero panels to the legal row. The only UI colour decision is ink-blue links, held consistently down to Cookie settings.
watch_out: Without art-directed photography of this grade, tiny labels and no CTAs read as an unfinished template.

name: The School for Temporary Liveness

type.note: Three faces with fixed roles: Helvetica for prose, Century for past volumes, Helvetica Black caps for the current one.

thesis: An experimental school's index page: four volumes, four dates, no chrome.
why_made: Emphasis comes from swapping typeface rather than colour or size, and the step from #fafafa to #fff is the only surface treatment.
watch_out: Pale #c0c0c0 type fails contrast, and without real substance behind it this reads as an unstyled placeholder.
