name: Per Appelgren

type.text: Neue Montreal, 22px/28px in DOM, about copy renders ~28px/36px
type.note: Wordmark is a separate Futura-style geometric bold with open tracking. Giant titles are absent from DOM measurement (max 22px); 2 canvases measured, so likely drawn in WebGL. Nothing sits between ~12px captions and ~295px titles.

thesis: A photographer's portfolio staged as a moving white gallery wall: a scatter of prints collapses into a deck, then into one pinned image at a time named by a giant client title.
why_made: The interface shrinks to three corner words and one disc arrow, leaving each motion beat (stack, scatter, deck, pin) room to land. One grotesk at two extremes gives scale contrast without any colour UI.
watch_out: Skewed cards and huge clipped type turn to noise if photos are uneven or the motion timing is loose.

name: Office Commun

type.note: Only 15px and 13px exist on the page; hierarchy comes from ink versus grey, never size.

thesis: A studio front page that fits in a screen and a half, made of a definition list, a pill nav and a wall of brand tiles.
why_made: One typeface at one size, with hierarchy coming only from ink versus grey, while every tile carries a complete brand world. The 4px and 999px radii are the only shapes.
watch_out: Without tiles of this standard, 15px Inter on near-white is simply an unstyled page.

name: HYDROFLOW

type.note: A mono face appears only in the tagline and testimonial names.

thesis: A tokenised water can launched like a techno product drop, with a metal can threaded through custom block type on graph paper.
why_made: The can sits between the headline lines instead of beside them, and the custom face gives the page an ownable voice. Outlined cells keep everything else disciplined.
watch_out: The display face is barely legible below 40px, and the FAQ carries investor-template questions that expose the filler copy.

name: Bakstad Construction

type.note: Two sizes only. Display line-height equals font size (30/30), and the stencil Didone appears solely as the logo.

thesis: A Seattle builder's site hung like a gallery wall: one stencil monogram, one hairline rail, and finished houses with air around them.
why_made: Two type sizes, two ink values and deliberately shifting image widths do all the work, while the stencil mark is the single authored flourish. Caption rows align exactly to image edges.
watch_out: Without top-grade architectural photography the empty field reads as an unfinished page.

name: Idea Bakery

type.note: Headlines change colour per slide; tracked caps eyebrows open each one.

thesis: A brand strategy consultancy that plays its baking metaphor straight, with handmade props filmed on candy-coloured sets.
why_made: The video props are properly art-directed, with real contact shadows and slow-motion physics, and each scroll step gets its own colour room.
watch_out: Yellow and purple type over pink props fails on contrast, and the rainbow UI colours and award ribbon date it quickly.

name: Spline

type.note: Geist Mono at 11-12px only for eyebrows, step labels and code; body leads at 18/28 in section intros.

thesis: A 3D design tool pitched to teams and agents on a pure black page where the real editor is the hero and the only colour is rendered content.
why_made: Interface language becomes design language: selection boxes, handles and named cursors appear in the headline and the cards. A three-step black ladder and strict Geist tracking stay quiet around live WebGL.
watch_out: With -3.36px tracking at small sizes or faked product panels, this collapses into generic dark AI SaaS.

name: Prägen Hätlen

type.note: Red Hat Mono 12px carries every label; the logo is a separate extended grotesque, reused huge in the footer.

thesis: A Swiss watch sold to crypto collectors as a scroll-driven teardown, where one render is pinned, exploded and inspected chapter by chapter.
why_made: One navy ladder, one periwinkle CTA and one bracketed mono label system hold 16,000px of scroll together. Renders are engineered down to the waffle dial while the interface stays tiny and 2px-radius around them.
watch_out: Without renders of this grade the scrub is just a slow page, and its unbacked fixed nav already collides with scrolled copy.

name: Telkom-OT

type.note: SF Mono handles nav, indices, kickers and the big numerals; Aeonik handles voice.

thesis: A die-casting toolmaker presented as an engineering drawing, where every section is a numbered, ruled sheet.
why_made: The 1.0 numbering, 1px rules, crop marks and wire linework all come from the trade, and one coral is kept for action and index. SF Mono and Aeonik split data from voice cleanly.
watch_out: Ruled cells, mono labels and crop marks on a brand with no technical content become sci-fi costume.

name: Clarisse Michard

type.note: The batch lists the name as an Adrien Quechon site; the page itself is Clarisse Michard, built by him.

thesis: A freelance designer's portfolio as a personality zine, mixing blackletter, pixels, pictograms and a palette-swap toggle.
why_made: Every gag is typeset with care: tight grotesque settings, exact pictogram alignment and a constant 32px frame keep the noise under control.
watch_out: Copied without the wit this is a pile of effects, and the inline icons and glitch portrait age quickly.

name: Overtime

type.note: No mid sizes: one 33px wordmark, everything else 11-12px mono.

thesis: A studio's themed image archive built around a live clock drawn at the scale of the page.

watch_out: The word list fades to near-invisible, and without a real idea behind it this is an empty white page with a stock image column.

name: Shinbu Aikido Club

type.note: Degular bold in 26-43px sets the Latin labels that overlap the kanji.

thesis: An aikido club's site as a sheet of riso-printed posters, where each navigation item is a card.
why_made: Three inks, one fixed shadow offset and shared grain unite very different cards, and each Latin-over-kanji lockup is composed individually.
watch_out: The overlaps hurt reading, and hard offset shadows on anything less graphic become a neo-brutalist template.

name: Concrete

why_made: The 24px dark frame, the cross-notched button and one dashed motif are the only authored details, and they are exact. Everything else is left to the two photographs.
watch_out: Dim the photos less or add a headline and it turns into a generic split hero.

name: Luis Henrique Bizarro

type.note: Only 19 characters of text on the page; the monogram does the display work.

thesis: A creative technologist's entry page that is one generative line drawing with two links.
why_made: One stroke weight unifies logo, ring and nav ticks, and the load animation shows the drawing being constructed rather than appearing.
watch_out: A splash page this empty lives or dies on the code running well, and it tells a visitor nothing until they click.

name: three.js

thesis: A library homepage with no pitch at all: a fixed mono link rail beside a wall of work made with the library.
why_made: The restraint is structural: one typeface, one blue, no gaps between tiles, so hundreds of unrelated project images read as a single surface.
watch_out: It only works with a huge supply of strong community imagery; with a dozen weak thumbnails it becomes an unstyled link dump.

name: Basement Studio

watch_out: Copy the 20/20 semibold body or the game-room hero without this content and it turns unreadable and gimmicky.

name: Cacao Bean Restaurant and Café

type.note: Three families: Instrument Serif heads, Jost body, ultra-wide Lexend Zetta for nav and buttons at 12-14px.

thesis: A local restaurant page that gets its structure from chocolate and blush colour blocks staggered behind food photography.
why_made: A palette pulled from one ingredient, plus blocks that overlap the photos, gives a WordPress build more composition than a stacked template.
watch_out: Stock-looking food shots and the small wide-tracked labels are what keep this silver; with weaker photos the blocks look like leftover placeholders.

name: LEA WINERY

type.note: One flared humanist family from 12px labels to the giant marquee. Statements ~34-46px. A consent modal covers the lower third of every frame in this capture.

thesis: A wine estate told as one continuous scroll, held in a fixed rail and header that recolour to match each section and bottle.
why_made: A single flared serif, cream ground and chrome that changes colour with the content make heavy Lenis and GSAP choreography feel like one considered object.
watch_out: Too many scrubbed effects at once, and the untinted blur over busy photos drops nav contrast, so copied without the restraint it becomes a motion demo.

name: Aniket

type.note: Scale is only 10, 12, 13, 14, 19. The H1s are 13px. Hierarchy comes from colour (#1d1d1f vs #6e6e73 vs #86868b), not size.

thesis: A personal page that is almost pure typography on four hairline rails, with one WebGL ribbon as its only flourish.
why_made: Everything hangs on rails only 7 percent black and sizes never exceed 19px, so the spacing and the single iridescent ribbon read as confident editing.
watch_out: At this size any sloppy spacing is exposed, and without the ribbon and real writing the page collapses into a plain text resume.

name: Michelle Kaye - Fine Arts

type.note: One family from 12px tracked caps to 115px, with oldstyle figures in the indexes.

thesis: An artist's site staged as a three-panel book, opened by a hand-written monogram and turned by deliberate scrolling.
why_made: A single serif, one dusty rose accent and small print-like details such as the offset hairline frame and numbered index give it a gallery catalogue feel.
watch_out: Cormorant plus cream plus a stock studio photo is a well-worn wedding-site look, and the small rose labels are at the edge of legible.

name: Queen's University Library

type.note: Card titles 28px 600. Navy #002452 and gold #fabd0f join crimson as full brand colours. Material Symbols for icons.

thesis: An institutional utility page that puts search, opening hours and live capacity first and lets three school colours organise the rest.
why_made: Practical components are given real thought, such as the notched arrow cards and live capacity rail, inside a consistent 24px radius system.
watch_out: Dense chrome, carousels everywhere and Open Sans keep it institutional; three saturated colours at equal strength will look like a template without strict tile rhythm.

name: YLEM

type.note: The 90px display face was not seen in this capture: only the counter and controls are on screen during the film.

thesis: A watch launch that withholds the site behind a full-screen exploded-view film with a progress counter.
why_made: The CGI is genuinely high end, and the interface is reduced to three small white labels, so the product has the whole viewport.
watch_out: A forced film before any content is a poor default, and without this render quality the percent counter just reads as a slow preloader.

name: Haikei

type.note: No web fonts. H2s 56/60 700, body sizes run large at 20-24px, secondary copy #bcc0c4 and #787d87.

thesis: A dark product landing page for a generator tool that uses its own SVG output as the page's illustration.
why_made: The real app window and generated shapes prove the product, and pill geometry, one violet and the same 48px margins keep it tidy.
watch_out: Centred headline, purple pill and icon-tile grid is the stock 2021 SaaS recipe; without the real product and generated art it looks generic.

name: JOBS - Soundtracks Youth Orchestra

type.note: Inner heads Playfair 56-72 at 600. Inter 11-12px uppercase with wide tracking for labels.

thesis: A youth orchestra site built like a concert programme: cinema-dark ground, a huge serif name and one curtain red.
why_made: The serif-and-Inter pairing, tight 2.4px radii, hairline tiles and a clear booking route give a small organisation a competent, serious system.
watch_out: Playfair on near-black with numbered bordered cards is close to a default AI-template look, and it relies on real concert photos to escape that.

name: Gagosian

type.note: Four faces with strict jobs: condensed caps headline for shouts, minion-pro-condensed bold 24-35 for titles and nav, minion-pro for reading and dates, GT America 13-16 for fair copy, credits and footer.

thesis: A gallery homepage run like a printed art periodical: strict three-column grid, four typefaces with assigned jobs, and art as the only colour.
why_made: Zero radii, no shadows and absolute grid discipline let wildly different artworks share a page. Every title, date and credit follows the same typographic rule.
watch_out: Without real art and rigorous editing the same grey nav and tiny outlined buttons look unfinished, and titles set straight on photos can lose legibility.

name: X8 Eyewear

type.note: Two scales only with nothing between: 13-15px narrow caps and 71-89px tight grotesque. No accent colour; the yellow corner ribbon is an award badge, not the brand.

thesis: An eyewear store that behaves like a lookbook, using black gutters, pinned spec panels and macro photography so the frames carry every screen.
why_made: Zero radii, zero shadows and two type sizes leave only image crop, gutter width and panel fill to do the work, and those are exact. Huge empty panels with copy pinned at the bottom give the products gallery-level room.
watch_out: The empty panels and tiny narrow caps only hold with studio-grade product photography; with ordinary images they read as an unfinished page.

name: Heart & Soil

type.note: Condensed high-contrast serif with italic emphasis, set against wide tracked caps. PT Mono is barely used.

thesis: A floral studio site built like printed stationery, from paper-textured colour blocks, a condensed serif and an engraved botanical crest.
why_made: Moss, cream, taupe and lavender all carry the same paper grain, and the 1px framed photos and hand-drawn crest tie every block to one printed object.
watch_out: Condensed serif at 1.4 leading plus paper textures slides into wedding-template territory without real photography and an original illustrated mark.

name: BCR Law LLP

type.note: 40px serif company names, 65px short names, 18px sans body. One accent per column: #3ed1f3, #e81246, #28d887, and a brown for Trust.

thesis: A professional services group whose homepage is one screen of four colour-coded columns, each a small identity for one company.
why_made: One column template repeats exactly, so four saturated hues read as a system; tonal titles, sheared monograms and bottom-aligned links keep it exact.
watch_out: Mid-tone titles on dark grounds fail contrast, as the brown Trust column shows; copy that palette without checking legibility and the page disappears.

name: The Philadelphia Orchestra

type.note: Heavy condensed caps at 24-60px over a friendly geometric sans. The stencil-like wordmark sets the slightly theatrical tone.

thesis: An orchestra site that sells the next concert first, wrapping event photography in heavy caps and hard bands of cream, violet and black.
why_made: It has a real content system: event card, news lead and feature row each repeat one structure, and electric violet makes classical music feel current.
watch_out: All-caps Roba needs short titles and stacked saturated bands need strong photos; the broken lead news image in this capture shows how fast it falls apart.

name: Athletics

type.display: Transitional serif (not in measured DOM text), ~120/~124px, regular, tight
type.note: Only 22px and 17px were measured, so serif sizes are estimates from frames. The serif-plus-one-sans binary carries all hierarchy.

thesis: A brand studio that uses one giant serif, one sans size and a logo-shaped video window, then lets client work supply the colour.
why_made: Text stays to two faces and essentially two sizes on charcoal, so saturated case work and a single lime break land hard. Near gold, but chips collide with the words they annotate and skewed cards are a loud move.
watch_out: Skewed cards and scattered chips turn gimmicky without first-rate client work behind them, and chips over a headline hide what it says.

name: Yuriy Vitrenko's Library

type.note: Geometric caps versus tight italic serif, with hairline drawings as the third voice. CeraCY supports the Cyrillic tags.

thesis: A personal document archive laid out as a ruled ledger, where wide caps, italic testimony and hairline drawings turn an energy dispute into a dossier.
why_made: A small grammar repeats exactly: ruled caps, italic text, boxed tags, one coral ellipse. The line drawings thread through the type instead of sitting beside it.
watch_out: The tilted ellipse and thin drawings look childish without strict grids around them, and placeholder book tiles expose how much the page depends on real images.

name: cagdascecen.com

type.note: Name set in a blurred heavy slab as a ghosted TV signal; Rajdhani for small headings. Amber marks live state and teal marks system text.

thesis: A media artist's portfolio disguised as an old TV broadcast, where projects are channels and the tree sculpture is the tuning surface.
why_made: The metaphor is carried through every control: line-up table, live clock, ON AIR flag, remote panel, scanlines. Sound is opt-in through a dialog with honest labels.
watch_out: Dim 12px mono on near-black is hard to read, and retro CRT styling without a concept behind it is pure costume.

name: Theatre Memory

type.note: One family at four sizes (20, 45, 90, 204) with nothing between them. Italic appears only for the project title in running text.

thesis: A national archive of theatre photography told as one sliding stack of prints, with huge grotesque type and years pinned to the corners of a white wall.
why_made: Four type sizes, four fixed anchor positions and pure black and white let the sepia objects provide all the colour and texture. Every screen has the composure of a museum wall label.
watch_out: A headline split by images only works when the word survives; with lesser pictures the pinned timeline becomes a long slideshow with hijacked scroll.

name: Claude

type.note: Serif for every heading and question, sans for labels, body and UI. Capture redirected to claude.com/product/overview.

thesis: An AI product page that swaps the usual dark glow for warm paper, a confident serif and small working demos framed around a person's day.
why_made: Warm whites step by tiny, deliberate amounts, every control shares one 8px radius and hairline, and each section has its own device (timeline, sentence selector, radial map) instead of another card grid.
watch_out: Warm serif on cream is now a common AI look; without the concrete demos and real restraint in colour it turns into a beige template.

name: CMBLU

type.note: A single family. Most capture stops show the hero only, so lower sections come from the two scroll frames.

thesis: An industrial battery maker that turns its solid-meets-flow chemistry into one macro video and two words pinned at opposite margins.
why_made: The hero concept is literal to the product, and the nav is a set of equal glass tiles aligned to the same margins as the headline pair.
watch_out: Dark macro video with glass tiles is a familiar climate-tech look; without a footage idea tied to the product it becomes a stock screensaver.

name: Area Technology

type.note: Only 11px live text exists on the page. All scale contrast comes from the wordmark against those tiny labels.

thesis: A visual technology studio whose site is one steel-blue wordmark and a white void, with a new absurdly polished object on every scroll.
why_made: The frame never changes, so each render lands as a full reveal. Quality of the objects, from tennis-ball fuzz to chrome mascots, is the entire argument.
watch_out: With average renders this is an empty page; Y2K chrome and neon only impress at this level of finish.

name: David Heckhoff

type.text: Urbanist, 14-22px; techno mono for HUD labels
type.note: Heavy rounded geometric sans matches the toy-like character. A slashed-zero mono appears only in the blue scan section.

thesis: A web developer's portfolio that follows a toy-like 3D self-portrait from a desk, through a hologram scanner, to a pile of parcels.
why_made: One character and one continuous camera connect every section, and the nav pill recolours for each scene, so the page behaves like a single WebGL set.
watch_out: Toy mascots and sci-fi HUD blue read juvenile outside a personal or game context, and the page hides everything behind a long 3D load.

name: Lacoste Ace Breaker

type.display: MonaSans, 140/147, 400, normal, uppercase, stacked under a serif LACOSTE wordmark
type.text: MonaSans, 18/19 weight 500 uppercase for small labels, 47/50 on the PLAY button
type.note: One sans plus the brand's high-contrast serif wordmark, nothing else.

thesis: A branded breakout game's start screen that explains the game with one ball-and-paddle glyph and a single huge PLAY button.
why_made: Court green, tennis yellow and cream are the only colours, and the mark, the loader and the button all reuse the same ball, so one screen feels fully art directed.
watch_out: Stripped of the bespoke ball glyph and the dark court plate, this is only two lines of text and a yellow pill.

name: USPS Delivers

type.note: The listed URL redirected to a generic USPS Delivers article, so this judges the content template only.

thesis: A corporate content hub that keeps long B2B articles calm with Helvetica, generous measure and federal red and blue used only as thin signals.
why_made: Commissioned illustration and a strict three-column related grid lift a plain template, and brand colour is limited to the CTA, a progress line and one sign-off rule.
watch_out: Light-weight Helvetica on white with soft stock images falls straight into forgettable corporate blog without the custom illustration.

name: Bauhaus Clock

type.note: One grotesque throughout; hierarchy comes from size and weight, and the footer wordmark runs at 215/258 weight 500, -3.225px.

thesis: Sells a $19 clock screensaver like a luxury watch, treating macro dial renders and native-quality settings panels as the product story.
why_made: Every surface obeys one 30px radius on a cool grey ground while colour lives only inside product tiles, and the sticky capsule, gloss CTA and ring selectors are tuned to the standard of native macOS chrome.
watch_out: Gloss buttons, frosted capsules and neumorphic toggles turn into dated skeuomorphism unless the renders beneath them are this detailed.

name: Now Code

type.note: Single rounded grotesque; two-tone weight of grey and white does the emphasis.

thesis: A French software consultancy that frames its pitch inside a notched dark panel and alternates charcoal sections with bright white cards.
why_made: The concave notch that docks three service cards into the hero is real geometry rather than a template stack, and a single muted red ties together logo, CTA and scribble.
watch_out: Stock office photos, AI isometric blog art and low-contrast grey subheads push this towards generic SaaS template; those need replacing before imitation.

name: Dalco

type.display: Tight neo-grotesque (unmeasured, capture lost fonts), ~48/56, light ~300, ~-1px
type.text: Same grotesque, ~20/28 and 16/22; mono eyebrows ~14px uppercase

thesis: A Swiss HPC hardware maker presented like a consumer tech launch, with an exploded server over a giant ghost marquee and gallery-lit product plates.
why_made: Sharp product renders on pale gradient plates and a mono-eyebrow system lift a technical catalogue, and the logo's arc reappears as the oxblood section's shape.
watch_out: The building image looks AI-made and the load sat black past 6s; heavy hero media with weak supporting imagery quickly undoes the premium feel.

name: Spring/Summer

type.display: Grotesk (compressed heavy), 386/290 H1 and 170/130 H2, 400, normal, uppercase
type.text: Montreal 18/25 .36px and 43/47.5 .86px lead; Supply mono 10-12px labels
type.note: Three tiers kept far apart: poster, grotesque reading text, tiny mono utility text.

thesis: An agency homepage run like a live dashboard, pairing a news-headline hero and poster type with a fixed utility rail while the whole page changes colour by section.
why_made: The theme flip is total, with nav, rail and type recolouring together, and poster-scale type is disciplined by a rigorous mono utility layer and 3px corners. Real client sites play inside full-bleed scenes.
watch_out: Poster type plus taped photos becomes a shouty zine without the calm cream ground, exact grid and tiny disciplined utility type.

name: TR Studio

type.display: Dia, 40/44, 400, normal, uppercase; corner letters are a drawn high-contrast serif ~70px tall
type.text: ABC humanist serif-sans ~24/36 for prose; Dia 14/16 uppercase for labels and 16/24 small copy
type.note: A drawn monogram, a quiet grotesque and a warm humanist text face; almost nothing sized in between.

thesis: An architecture studio's site where the monogram stays pinned to the viewport corners and projects drift through a bone-coloured frame like rooms seen through a doorway.
why_made: Four fixed corners, two rotated labels and one centre axis hold the page, so photographs can vary freely, and colour steps from bone to oxblood to periwinkle with no radii, shadows or rules.
watch_out: Without top-tier interior photography and a properly drawn monogram, the empty frame looks unfinished and the centred axis looks like a wedding template.

name: FWA Wire

type.note: Period-correct pair: bitmap face for chrome, Verdana for reading, nothing above 15px.

thesis: A 2026 winners' newswire deliberately rebuilt as a 2001 Flash-era portal, with a fixed 924px column of bevelled black modules, pixel type and hazard yellow.
why_made: It commits to the period with total consistency: fixed width, hard corners, tiny bitmap labels, corner ticks, and it still reads as a working information-dense feed.
watch_out: As nostalgia pastiche it depends on the FWA's history; 6-8px yellow-on-black type fails legibility and would look broken on any ordinary brief.

name: The 2026 ADCC Awards

type.display: PP Neue Montreal as drawn lettering, ~118px cap height, regular, normal, uppercase
type.text: PP Neue Montreal, 16/24 body, 32/38 700 uppercase H2
type.note: The hero is lettering artwork; live text stops at 32px.

thesis: An awards entry page that spends everything on one typographic stair-step hero and keeps the rest as plain information.
why_made: The 3-column letter pyramid is a real idea: it fills the width edge to edge and reads as an 'elevate' gesture, and the square monogram echoes the same building-block logic.
watch_out: Below the hero it is default Bootstrap: #0d6efd links and button, dropdown carets, centred dates. Copy the hero, not the page beneath.

name: Bohdan Ratiiev: Born From Code

type.text: Geist Mono, 12-16 uppercase, ~14.5 leading on annotations; Caslon 44/53 for prose
type.note: Condensed-feeling Caslon against system-log mono; only black on white.

thesis: A designer's portfolio staged as a system printout, with Caslon sentences plotted on a dot grid among scattered mono annotations and an ASCII monkey.
why_made: Two typefaces in black on white, exact mono indentation and a plotted dot field make randomness feel engineered, and every interaction (scramble, hover, boxed word) is typographic.
watch_out: Fake terminal annotations and ASCII art are pure decoration; copied loosely, without this exact typography, they read as hacker cosplay.

name: Reformation

type.display: Newtime R bold wordmark ~100px; TimesNow 48/62, 400, normal
type.note: Lowercase UI, a heavy geometric wordmark and Times-style serif lines with dry copy. Phone frames hit a Cloudflare check, so only desktop was judged.

thesis: A fashion store that lets flat black type and strong campaign photography do the selling, with lowercase nav and dry jokes as the personality.
why_made: Zero radii, no shadows and 1px seams between images make the grid feel like a lookbook, while a cropped heavy wordmark and Times serif give it an unmistakable voice.
watch_out: Lowercase, cropped wordmarks and zero radius look confident only with art-directed photography; over ordinary product shots they look unfinished.

name: Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts

type.display: GT America Condensed, 96/96, 500, normal, uppercase; section heads 56 and hero 66
type.note: One superfamily: condensed caps for all headings, regular width for reading.

thesis: A civic museum homepage that turns the slash in its logo into the page's single geometric idea, cutting the hero, dividers and info strip at one angle.
why_made: Slate ink, one terracotta and a sand band keep a very busy programme orderly, and a single condensed grotesque carries every heading from hero to footer.
watch_out: The hero video never resolved in this capture, leaving a black pane and spinner; slanted panels that depend on heavy video look broken when it fails.

name: PURHO

type.display: purho-med (neo-grotesque), 76/75, weight 400 file reading as bold, +1px
type.note: Only two jobs for type: a 76px voice and a 15px legal line. The cookie notice covers the top 272px of most captured frames; load-1 shows the clean state.

thesis: A Murano glass brand tells its whole story as one display-size paragraph on charcoal, then ends on outlined links over macro glass video.
why_made: Refusing a hero image and letting 76px copy run edge to edge is the entire idea, and swapping single nouns to 1px outline gives it rhythm with no second colour.
watch_out: Outlined words fail in a heavy cut or at small sizes, and display-size copy only works if the writing is short and good.

name: Effepinna Studio

type.note: A single red for all type on white. 50/49 bold work titles, 20px meta, 15px lists. The hero wordmark is the same family at heavy weight.

thesis: An Italian art director's portfolio in one red on white, led by a caricature of himself who stands, then tumbles, through the page.
why_made: One ink colour, hairline red rules and a single family let loud AI imagery and a cartoon body sit inside a strict poster layout.
watch_out: Red body text on white is tiring beyond a few lines, and the character becomes a gimmick without a real graphic voice around it.

name: Linear

type.display: Inter Variable, 64/64 hero and 72/72 closing, weight 510, -0.022em
type.note: Weight 510 not 500 or 600. Section heads 48/48, ledes 24/32, nav 13-14px, Berkeley Mono at 10-13px for fig labels, dates, file paths and code.

thesis: A near-black page where real, recreated product UI does the selling, held together by one half-page split and full-bleed hairlines.
why_made: Every panel is live DOM UI masked into the dark instead of a screenshot, and the ladder of greys, 510 weight and strict x=80 / x=752 alignment leave nothing loose.
watch_out: Copy the darkness without the believable product content and it collapses into an empty dark template with grey text.

name: STUDIO UNLMTD

type.display: Inter Tight, 150/135 hero and 172.8/155.5 close, weight 900, -5.26 to -7.78px
type.note: Mid-level heads ~62/74 at ~600 with -0.04em. 10-12px uppercase tracked labels carry all the small structure.

thesis: A Swiss AI-assisted agency built from black Inter Tight 900 slabs where one word per section is filled with a live flowing gradient.
why_made: Gradient is rationed to one word per screen, and everything around it is a disciplined grid of 1px rules, tracked labels and hard black and white slabs.
watch_out: Gradient text is one step from cheap: use it twice on a screen or on small sizes, and it reads as stock AI-startup styling.

name: Elyx

type.note: Three voices: bold serif questions, Söhne 600 ~64/70 statements, Tiempos 400 64-80 on dark. Body stays wide at ~24px, more essay than landing page.

thesis: A product launch written as an essay: warm paper with hand-drawn marks argues the problem, then the page goes dark and the product is named.
why_made: Everything is typography and a few hand-made marks, with the brand's spectral gradient rationed to a hairline, a word or the final horizon. The pacing is what feels expensive.
watch_out: Scribbles look childish if they are vector-perfect or everywhere, and this page needs genuinely good writing because there is no product UI to lean on.

name: Yamauchi No.10 Family Office

type.note: Measured Times 16px is hidden DOM; all visible type is drawn in WebGL.

thesis: A family office entry gate drawn as a dot-matrix LED sign, with red, green, blue and yellow pixels raining through a grey tile logo.
why_made: A strict 16px cell governs every element, from the tile logo to the rain, so a playful gimmick still feels exact and engineered.
watch_out: It is an entrance gate with sound, not a page: the same trick hides all real content and its phone crop cuts the logo off.

name: Driftime Impact Report 2022

type.note: Only four sizes on the whole page: 20, 30, 60, 100. Chapter titles are custom SVG condensed caps with one swashed ribbon letter.

thesis: A studio's annual report paced like a printed magazine, with each chapter its own colour room and a custom ribbon-letter title.
why_made: A four-size type scale and fixed column rules stay constant while colour and titles change, so 67,000px of scrolling feels edited rather than long.
watch_out: The ribbon letters only work as drawn lettering at full width, and the fixed rules look like table borders if they are heavy or always on.

name: ECI

type.note: H2 102/97, section titles ~52/52, statements Akkurat 42/52. Akkurat Mono only for the superscript indices. All body and nav at 20px, larger than usual.

thesis: A climate-AI endowment that pairs a tightly tracked deck serif with rounded frames of Earth footage and a numbered, almost archival nav.
why_made: Serif, grotesk and mono each have one job, greens come from a tight three-step ramp, and every section repeats the same 32px gutters, 20px frames and black rule.
watch_out: The tracked-in serif turns fussy below ~50px, and stock nature imagery without this restraint falls straight into greenwashing cliché.

name: Benzo the Great Developer

type.display: Benguiat Bold Condensed BT, ~56px, weight 400, normal tracking
type.note: White display, gold #e2c06d body, white run-in leads. Helvetica appears only on the wall label, as a joke.

thesis: A developer portfolio staged as a haunted magician's painting: the whole site scrolls inside a fixed carved picture frame.
why_made: A full commission of painted art plus one rigid conceit, including wall label and frame, means nothing looks like a theme, and period type holds to the character.
watch_out: Without bespoke illustration the conceit is pure kitsch, and the logo wall of famous clients and all-gold body copy are hard to read outside this world.

name: Language Explorer

type.note: Largest DOM text measured 18px, so the headline size is an estimate. Google Sans Mono 10-12px for world stats and system notes.

thesis: A full-screen particle globe where each light is a language, with a calm search-first interface floating over it.
why_made: All drama sits in the depth-of-field render while the UI stays a sober outlined Google kit in white, grey and one blue underline.
watch_out: Text set directly over bright particles loses legibility, and a glowing globe is a heavy, overused cliché unless the points are real data.

name: Stripe

type.note: One family at weight 300 for all display sizes; hierarchy comes from ink colour, not weight.

thesis: A very dense financial platform page kept calm by one light typeface, visible page rails, and a single flowing colour ribbon.
why_made: Every block sits on the same two rails and the two-tone sentence heading repeats throughout, so 15,000px reads as one system. Product art is real checkout UI at believable fidelity, not illustration.
watch_out: The ribbon without its fine etched striations and without real UI beside it becomes a generic rainbow blob.

name: Pete Sena

type.display: Inter Tight, 62-66/~1.1 weight 400, -1.55px; 311px footer word at -18.7px
type.note: Single family; panels change colour rather than type.

thesis: A personal site for a founder-advisor that alternates black statements with hard-edged colour panels stacking over each other.
why_made: Panels share one two-column template, so loud colour stays orderly, and the principle dial gives the page a memorable pinned moment.
watch_out: The bottom pill collides with panel copy and CTAs, and stock talking-head tiles look amateur if not graded.

name: Daylight

type.note: 12px uppercase tracked Styrene on buttons and step chips.

thesis: A mental-health clinic page coloured as one continuous sunrise, with a warm serif and inked line drawings replacing clinical blue.
why_made: The single gradient across all sections gives identity, and the stippled illustrations are specific to the subject.
watch_out: Stock family photos and saturated gold can tip it into a template; the gradient needs real tonal steps, not one yellow fade.

name: New Material

type.note: Nothing exceeds 26px after the intro; the card deck supplies the scale.

thesis: A studio site that replaces headlines with a shuffled deck of work, where each project recolours the small interface around it.
why_made: Type stays at one size in two inks, so hierarchy comes from grey vs dark and soft bloom elevation. Small objects such as the speech bubble, one-question form and focus-pulled portraits each have a specific idea.
watch_out: Blur, bloom and grey-on-white go limp and illegible without strong media in the cards.

name: Ueno

type.note: Helvetica Neue bold only for nav and one label.

thesis: A short studio page run almost entirely in one serif, where client names become the logo wall and the about text is the content.
why_made: One serif at three sizes, black on white, trusts the writing. The typeset client marquee turns a commodity section into typography.
watch_out: Serif plus white is thin without real credentials and film; on a generic studio this reads empty.

name: Wild

type.note: Six-digit dates such as 230626 used as date stamps.

thesis: A studio home that is one sideways rail of tall work images, with its intro and news stream slotted between them as just another column.
why_made: Strong renders at a single portrait format and a 2px radius on everything make the rail feel like one object.
watch_out: Page has no vertical structure, so it depends on image quality, and the cookie card here covers the bottom right of the rail.

name: Fantasy

type.note: Almost no interface type; a handful of short lines over film.

thesis: An agency reel built as one long dark film, where scroll moves through blurred chapters of product renders and copy is reduced to a few lines.
why_made: Interface is cut to a mark, a chip and a small tag, so the film carries the page. The final hard cut to white gives the long dark run an ending.
watch_out: On weak media this is just a slow black page, and blur transitions hide content from anyone scrolling quickly.

name: Fora

type.note: A single custom serif logotype is the only contrast to the grotesk.

thesis: A strategy consultancy whose whole site is one fixed six-cell poster, mixing flat colour, a serif logotype and two photographs.
why_made: Terracotta, lilac and sky are picked from the photographs, and everything is locked to the same 25px inset.
watch_out: It works as one screen only; add scrolling sections or a fourth colour and the poster logic falls apart.

name: KAWARA MUSEUM - LIBRARY

type.text: Shuei KakuGo Gin B, 16/30, tracked; Outfit for Latin
type.note: Generous tracking and vertical setting for chapter marks.

thesis: A municipal tile museum whose whole interface is made from its subject: roof-tile friezes, fired clay textures and paper ground.
why_made: Every decorative shape comes from the collection, and chapters hold one layout so a dense public site stays navigable.
watch_out: Clip shapes, mascots and textures become childish without a tight palette and consistent section template.

name: AuthKit

type.note: ibmPlexMono only for the inline command and terminal.

thesis: An auth product page that shows the sign-in box itself as the hero, then proves depth with tiny exact UI inside a ruled page frame.
why_made: The hairline frame, nested tray-and-panel UI and scanline motif recur from hero to compliance badges. Colour is rationed to one indigo button and a dusk gradient.
watch_out: Tight -3px tracking and skeleton UI read as a template if the mini UIs are not real product states.

name: SUTÉRA

type.note: Two extremes only: huge tight grotesk and tiny caps mono.

thesis: A designer portfolio staged as an annotated specimen sheet, with renders and stickers placed into sentences and technical callouts pinned to a white grid.
why_made: A strict crosshair grid and one mono size hold many collaged objects together, and every leader line lands on a real node.
watch_out: Without the grid and restraint in the mono, inline stickers and floating renders collapse into AI-collage clutter.

name: Stone Island

type.note: One family at one size across the whole page, with Light, Regular and Medium files loaded. No UI accent colour; all colour comes from photography. One flaw: left and right nav text sit ~3px apart vertically (y60 vs y63).

thesis: A fashion house typed like an equipment spec sheet: one mono at 14px over viewport-tall campaign photographs and hard black and white flips.
why_made: The restraint is total and measurable: one family, one size, no radii, no shadows, and a 22px margin with 12px gutter grid that CTAs honour across sections. Hierarchy comes only from weight and case, so photographs and the compass mark carry all the scale.
watch_out: Small mono over dimmed photos only holds with art-directed imagery; with stock shots it becomes a dark template with hard-to-read captions.

name: George Thomas Hatton

type.note: Pure black on white with no grey tier or accent; the greys in the pixel palette are antialiasing. 10px uppercase labels are the only second size. Capture ended early, so no phone frames exist, but the page itself is a single 900px sheet with no scroll.

thesis: A portfolio that declines to be one: a single unscrolling sheet of 12px bold text set like a printed credits page, with work available on request.
why_made: One font and weight, 1.2 leading, one 10px label tier, and a 10px margin from which four columns hang on one top line, so placement does all the work. The asymmetric jump from bio to lists supplies the tension.
watch_out: Without real client names and a sharp grotesque this is just an unstyled page, and 12px bold becomes tiring beyond a single screen.

name: International Magic

type.note: Measured sizes are only 32, 15 and 11px. The ~120/124px intro title is estimated from load frames because it is gone before measurement. No accent; all colour comes from client work.

thesis: A studio reel built as one long pinned stack: pale chrome with two matched 56px trays stays fixed while client images and loops pass between them.
why_made: The viewport is divided exactly (16/56/16/724/16/56/16), so media fits flush between the trays, and one 3px radius plus one font at three sizes runs the whole system. Frosted trays tint from the work beneath, so the chrome stays quiet without looking detached.
watch_out: Without strong client work the 66,605px stack becomes a slow scroll past average pictures, and frame heights must follow the viewport or media collides with the trays.
